column5: Everything is burning. I can do little to stop it from spreading.{w}\nAn immense pain assaults my head, and I throw my face into my hands.{w}\nThe same question repeatedly plays in my mind: \"What am I doing here...?\"
column6: 一切都在燃烧，我几乎无力阻止火势蔓延。{w}\n一阵剧痛袭上头顶，我双手掩面。{w}\n同一个问题在我脑中反复回响：“我为什么会在这里……？”

column5: I have no knowledge of what happened up until this point.{w}\nMy brain is struggling to fill in the blanks, not gaining any headway.{w}\nIt was almost like, until this exact moment, I never existed.
column6: 在此之前发生了什么，我一无所知。{w}\n我的大脑拼命想填补这些空白，却毫无进展。{w}\n就好像，直到这一刻之前，我从未存在过一样。

column5: Then why is it {i}now{/i} that cognition has found me?{w}\nWas there something I could do to put out these flames?{w}\nOr perhaps, was I the cause of this inferno to begin with?
column6: 那么，为何偏偏是{i}现在{/i}，意识才找到了我？{w}\n我是否有办法扑灭这些火焰？{w}\n又或者，这场大火最初就是由我引起的？

column5: A foolish thought, and one I throw away.{w}\nIf I was responsible, then I wouldn't feel this sense of dread.{w}\nAn emotion shared by those who stand beside me.
column6: 这是个愚蠢的念头，我把它抛开。{w}\n若真是我造成的，我便不会感到这种恐惧。{w}\n一种站在我身旁之人也同样怀有的情绪。

column5: Come on, pick up the pace...!\nIf we waste any more time, we won't make it out alive!\nThere's no way the Elder would let me live that one down.
column6: 快，加快脚步……！\n要是再浪费时间，我们就别想活着出去了！\n长老绝不会让我把这事轻易揭过去的。

column5: Are you even paying attention!?
column6: 你到底有没有在听！？

column5: What!? I know who you are, Seeress!\nDid you hit your head or something...?
column6: 什么！？我当然知道你是谁，先知！\n你是撞到头了吗……？

column5: I know who you are, Seer!\nDid you hit your head or something...?
column6: 我知道你是谁，先知！\n你是撞到头了吗……？

column5: She scoffs as she turns the other way.{w}\nBut I know she's right. I'm not taking this seriously.{w}\nIt feels like a dream, and I doubt that it's all happening.
column6: 她哼了一声，把头转向另一边。{w}\n但我知道她说得对，我根本没把这一切当回事。{w}\n这一切像一场梦，我怀疑它是否真的在发生。

column5: A few moments later, a sudden sensation startles me.{w}\nThere's a firm grip on my shoulder. We aren't alone.{w}\nUnderneath a veil of fright, I turn to greet this second stranger.
column6: 片刻之后，一阵突如其来的触感吓了我一跳。{w}\n有只手牢牢抓住了我的肩膀。我们并非孤身一人。{w}\n我怀着满心惊恐，转头去迎接这第二个陌生人。

column5: Valessa has our safety in mind, okay?\nForgive her hot-headedness for me.\nFreedom isn't too much farther.
column6: 瓦莱莎是在为我们的安危着想，明白吗？\n替我原谅她的一时冲动吧。\n自由就快到了。

column5: We need to stay calm and think this through.\nTwo guys like us? We should have no problem.\nWe'll be safe and sound before you know it.
column6: 我们得保持冷静，好好想清楚。\n像我们这样的两个大男人？肯定没问题。\n转眼之间我们就能平安无事。

column5: Valessa has our safety in mind, okay?\nForgive her hot-headedness for me.\nFreedom isn't too much farther.
column6: 瓦莱莎是在为我们的安危着想，明白吗？\n替我原谅她的一时冲动吧。\n自由就快到了。

column5: We need to stay calm and think this through.\nTwo girls like you? I'm sure you can come up with something.\nWe'll be safe and sound before you know it.
column6: 我们得保持冷静，好好想清楚。\n像你们这样的两个姑娘？我相信你们能想出办法。\n转眼之间我们就能平安无事。

column5: We weave through the houses and alleys to remain unseen.{w}\nDoing our best to be completely silent, we bring no attention to ourselves.{w}\nThe flames encourage our urgency, but we're careful not to be fast or reckless.
column6: 我们在房屋与小巷间穿行，避开别人的视线。{w}\n我们竭力保持安静，不引来任何注意。{w}\n火焰催促着我们加快脚步，但我们小心不让自己过快或过于鲁莽。

column5: Our silence makes everything else more prominent, however.{w}\nThe screams of those being slaughtered fill me with a feeling of disgust.{w}\nWe need to find cover, and Valessa points out a small alcove waiting nearby.
column6: 然而，这份寂静反而让其他一切更加醒目。{w}\n被杀之人的惨叫声让我心中充满厌恶。{w}\n我们需要找个藏身处，瓦莱莎指了指附近一个现成的小壁龛。

column5: Look. They're dying because they panicked.\nWe need to stay calm and think through this together.\nIf we freak out, we'll only end up like them, you know?
column6: 看吧。他们之所以会死，是因为慌了神。\n我们必须保持冷静，一起把这事想清楚。\n要是我们也慌了，下场只会和他们一样，懂吗？

column5: She has a point.\nOur first instinct was to run, but so was theirs.\nWe should let them face the brunt of this attack.
column6: 她说得有道理。\n我们的第一反应是逃跑，可他们也是。\n我们应该让他们去承受这次进攻的主力。

column5: What else are we supposed to do?\nWe're not equipped to take them on alone.
column6: 不然我们还能怎么办？\n我们没那个本事单独对付他们。

column5: But using them like pawns, Ulric?\nThe people of Valinorth deserve more than that!
column6: 可把他们当棋子利用，乌尔里克？\n瓦利诺斯的人民不该被这样对待！

column5: Do you have any better ideas!?\nIf we try to save them all, we'll die.\nI'm here to protect you two, not kill you.
column6: 你有更好的办法吗！？\n要是我们想救下所有人，我们自己就会死。\n我来这里是保护你们俩的，不是来害死你们的。

column5: Good to know we're on the same page.\nIt'd be foolish to try taking them on alone.
column6: 很高兴我们想法一致。\n单枪匹马去对付他们，那是愚蠢之举。

column5: But that means you're using them as pawns, Ulric!\nI can't let you do that to the people of Valinorth!
column6: 但那就意味着你在把他们当棋子，乌尔里克！\n我不能让你这样对待瓦利诺斯的人民！

column5: Do you have any better ideas!?\nIf we try to save them all, we'll die.\nI'm here to protect you two, not kill you.
column6: 你有更好的办法吗！？\n要是我们想救下所有人，我们自己就会死。\n我来这里是保护你们俩的，不是来害死你们的。

column5: I agree, Ulric. We can't sacrifice everyone to buy time.\nI think the people of Valinorth deserve far better!
column6: 我同意，乌尔里克。我们不能用牺牲所有人来争取时间。\n我觉得瓦利诺斯的人民值得更好的对待！

column5: Would you rather perish with them, Valessa?\nThat's what'll happen if you go running out there.\nWe're not equipped to handle this on our own.
column6: 你宁愿和他们一起死吗，瓦莱莎？\n你要是冲出去，结果就是这样。\n凭我们自己是应付不来的。

column5: You have to remember what I'm doing here!\nIt's my job to protect the both of you.\nEveryone else is expendable.
column6: 你可得记住我来这儿是干什么的！\n我的职责就是保护你们俩。\n其他人都可以牺牲。

column5: My suspicions are correct. Ulric is the one protecting us.{w}\nBut why exactly are we a higher priority than the civilians?{w}\nI venture a guess that we're currently in this \"Valinorth\".
column6: 我的猜测没错，保护我们的人是乌尔里克。{w}\n可为什么我们的优先级会比平民还高？{w}\n我大胆猜测，我们现在就在这个“瓦利诺斯”。

column5: The pain in my head pulses again, and I stumble back.{w}\nAs I let out a groan, Ulric rushes over to my side.{w}\nHis exaggerated concern is now understandable.
column6: 头上的剧痛再次阵阵袭来，我踉跄着后退。{w}\n我发出一声呻吟，乌尔里克立刻冲到我身边。{w}\n他这份夸张的关切，如今总算说得通了。

column5: It must be the smoke. Make sure to sit down.\nThe lower you are right now, the better.\nAre you having trouble breathing?
column6: 一定是烟熏的。快坐下。\n你现在位置越低越好。\n呼吸有困难吗？

column5: I shake my head, and let him know that it's not the smoke.{w}\nThis causes Valessa to chime in, voicing her concerns as well.
column6: 我摇摇头，告诉他不是烟熏的缘故。{w}\n这让瓦莱莎也插了进来，说出她的担忧。

column5: Yeah, something else is going on here.\nHe's been acting strange for a while now.
column6: 是啊，这里面另有蹊跷。\n他最近一直表现得很古怪。

column5: Yeah, something else is going on here.\nShe's been acting strange for a while now.
column6: 是啊，这里面另有蹊跷。\n她最近一直表现得很古怪。

column5: Is there something you need to tell us?
column6: 你有什么事要告诉我们吗？

column5: Join the club.\nIt's not like we anticipated this.\nCome on, time to gear you up.
column6: 大家都一样。\n我们也没料到会这样。\n来吧，该给你配点装备了。

column5: Did some debris fall on your head back there?\nI'm starting to side with Valessa on this one.\nCome on, time to gear you up.
column6: 刚才是不是有碎石砸到你脑袋了？\n这件事我开始站瓦莱莎这边了。\n来吧，该给你配点装备了。

column5: He steps away for a few moments, and inspects the ground around him.{w}\nThere's a brief period where I can't see him, but he returns with a blade.{w}\nThe fire causes it to glisten, almost like it's begging me to take it.
column6: 他走开了一会儿，仔细打量着四周的地面。{w}\n有那么短短一阵我看不见他，等他回来时手上多了一把剑。{w}\n火光映得剑身闪闪发亮，仿佛在恳求我把它拿走。

column5: I don't care what's going on in that head of yours.\nBut it's not more important than your survival.\nWe're all overwhelmed, it's not just you.
column6: 我才不管你那脑袋里在想些什么。\n但那比不上保住你的命重要。\n我们都快撑不住了，不只你一个。

column5: He holds out the blade, expecting my compliance.{w}\nAt this rate, it seems like fighting may be inevitable.
column6: 他把剑递过来，等着我乖乖接过。{w}\n照这样下去，恐怕一战在所难免。

column5: Take it. We won't be standing here forever.\nAs soon as we leave this alcove, we'll be vulnerable.\nI can't take care of you all the time, you know.
column6: 拿着。我们不会一直站在这儿。\n一旦离开这个壁龛，我们就毫无掩护。\n我可没法时时刻刻照看你，你知道的。

column5: You must be mistaken. This wasn't an option.\nI can't keep an eye on both of you in the heat of battle.\nValessa has her daggers, and you need something as well.
column6: 你一定是误会了。这可不是商量。\n战况激烈时，我没法同时照看你们两个。\n瓦莱莎有她的匕首，你也得有件武器。

column5: He grabs my hand and places the blade in my grasp.{w}\nHe's strong enough that I knew resisting was worthless.{w}\nIt's probably better not to fight, so I take it and nod.
column6: 他抓住我的手，把剑塞进我手里。{w}\n他的力气大得让我明白反抗毫无意义。{w}\n最好还是别较劲，于是我接过剑，点了点头。

column5: Now that's what I like to hear.\nI'll feel better if you have something to fight with.\nValessa has her daggers, but you had nothing.
column6: 这才像话。\n你手里有武器，我会安心些。\n瓦莱莎有她的匕首，你却什么都没有。

column5: I grab the blade and swing it a couple times, testing its weight.{w}\nIt seems good enough for me, and I wouldn't have any problems using it.{w}\nThough it was a far cry from the massive blade that Ulric carried.
column6: 我握住剑，挥了两下，试试它的重量。{w}\n手感还不错，用起来应该没问题。{w}\n只是和乌尔里克背着的那把巨剑比起来，差得远了。

column5: Now then, it's time to move.\nSeems like some of the noise has finally died down.\nWe should start by investigating the town square.
column6: 那么，该动身了。\n外面的动静似乎终于小了些。\n我们先去城镇广场看看吧。

column5: He walks off, expecting us to follow along.{w}\nBut as I'm about to take a step, Valessa grabs my arm.{w}\nThe look on her face tells me something is wrong.
column6: 他抬脚走了，等着我们跟上。{w}\n可我刚要迈步，瓦莱莎抓住了我的手臂。{w}\n她脸上的神情告诉我，出事了。

column5: You're confused about all this, right?\nI bet you don't even know what being the \"Seer\" means.\nOr how we've known each other for our entire lives...
column6: 你对这一切都很困惑，对吧？\n我猜你连“先知”意味着什么都不知道。\n也不知道我们俩从小就相识……

column5: You're confused about all this, right?\nI bet you don't even know what being the \"Seeress\" means.\nOr how we've known each other for our entire lives...
column6: 你对这一切都很困惑，对吧？\n我猜你连“先知”意味着什么都不知道。\n也不知道我们俩从小就相识……

column5: I look at the ground in both shame and confusion.{w}\nShe's completely right, my head is a mess.{w}\nAs I try to think of an excuse, her response surprises me.
column6: 我既羞愧又困惑地低下头。{w}\n她说得一点没错，我的脑子乱成一团。{w}\n我正想找借口，她的反应却出乎我的意料。

column5: That's normal, but please listen.\nWe only have a few moments before Ulric notices we're not there.\nThe Seer is special. You wield spirits to induce prophetic visions.
column6: 这很正常，但请听我说。\n我们只有一小会儿，很快乌尔里克就会发现我们没跟上。\n先知很特别。你御使灵，以此引出预言的幻象。

column5: That's normal, but please listen.\nWe only have a few moments before Ulric notices we're not there.\nThe Seeress is special. You wield spirits to induce prophetic visions.
column6: 这很正常，但请听我说。\n我们只有一小会儿，很快乌尔里克就会发现我们没跟上。\n先知很特别。你御使灵，以此引出预言的幻象。

column5: When you have these visions, you're unable to remember anything.\nWhen you wake up, you'll dismiss it as a dream and forget it ever happened.\nAs your Scribe, it's my job to help you take advantage of this.
column6: 当你身处这些幻象中时，什么都记不住。\n醒来后，你会把它当成一场梦抛诸脑后，忘记它曾发生过。\n作为你的书记官，我的职责就是帮你利用这一点。

column5: We have to follow Ulric now, but know {i}one{/i} thing.\nThe way you're acting. I'm certain this is a vision.\nThat means you can use it for information.
column6: 我们现在得跟上乌尔里克了，但你只需记住{i}一点{/i}。\n看你的举止，我确信这是一场幻象。\n也就是说，你可以利用它来获取情报。

column5: She takes a few steps closer to me, and grabs my hands.{w}\nStaring right in my eyes, I notice a glimmer of hope shining within her.
column6: 她朝我走近几步，握住我的双手。{w}\n她直直凝视着我的眼睛，我注意到她眼底闪烁着的一线希望。

column5: I'm relieved. This means Valinorth is still fine!\nWhen you wake up, use this vision to save everyone.\nIt's your duty as Seer to ensure this doesn't become real!
column6: 我松了口气。这说明瓦利诺斯还好好的！\n等你醒来，就用这场幻象去救所有人。\n作为先知，你的职责就是确保这一切不会成真！

column5: I'm relieved. This means Valinorth is still fine!\nWhen you wake up, use this vision to save everyone.\nIt's your duty as Seeress to ensure this doesn't become real!
column6: 我松了口气。这说明瓦利诺斯还好好的！\n等你醒来，就用这场幻象去救所有人。\n作为先知，你的职责就是确保这一切不会成真！

column5: She lets go of my hands, and follows after Ulric.{w}\nThough it's hard to believe what she said, I'm less confused.{w}\nI finally had a reason for why I felt so \"disconnected\".
column6: 她松开我的手，跟上了乌尔里克。{w}\n虽然她的话很难让人相信，但我没那么困惑了。{w}\n我终于明白自己为何会有那种“格格不入”的感觉。

column5: But if this was a vision, then what would become of Ulric and Valessa?{w}\nWould all of this carnage be undone as soon as I woke up?{w}\nWhat if they died — or what if I died in this vision?
column6: 可如果这是一场幻象，那乌尔里克和瓦莱莎又会怎样？{w}\n我一醒来，这场屠杀就会全部烟消云散吗？{w}\n要是他们死了呢——或者，要是“我”在这场幻象中死了呢？

column5: I follow after Valessa, realizing I might never know.{w}\nBut a faint sense of determination rises up within me.{w}\nIf there was a chance I could stop this? I had to do it.
column6: 我跟上瓦莱莎，意识到自己也许永远无从得知。{w}\n但一股淡淡的决心在我心中升起。{w}\n只要有一线机会阻止这一切，我就必须去做。

column5: In the present day, The Triumvirate conspires with their Grand Inquisitor.{w}\nFor the events that led to Valinorth's destruction had yet to be set in motion.{w}\nSovy knelt before his masters, more eager to serve than he had ever been before.
column6: 而在当下，三人执政团正与他们的大审判官密谋。{w}\n因为导致瓦利诺斯覆灭的事件，此时尚未拉开序幕。{w}\n索维跪在他的主人们面前，比以往任何时候都更渴望效命。

column5: Rise, Sovy.\nBut please, assure us of your certainty.\nWe'd hate to act without knowing everything.
column6: 起来吧，索维。\n但请你让我们确信万无一失。\n我们不愿在一切未明之前贸然行动。

column5: The prisoner mentions \"Valinorth\" over and over.\nThe Rebels are hiding something of importance there.\nAlong with recent events, we can only surmise one thing.
column6: 那囚犯一遍又一遍地提到“瓦利诺斯”。\n反抗军在那里藏了某样重要的东西。\n结合近来发生的事，我们只能推断出一件事。

column5: The Blade of Exodus?
column6: 流亡之刃？

column5: I am almost certain.\nBut if that's where they've chosen to hide it?\nIt means that our other target is also there.
column6: 我几乎可以确定。\n但要是他们选择把它藏在哪儿？\n那就意味着我们的另一个目标也在那里。

column5: Your compliance pleases us, Sovy.\nYour plan was risky, but it worked out in the end.\nA final interrogation would influence our decision further.
column6: 你的顺从让我们很满意，索维。\n你的计划虽有风险，但最终还是奏效了。\n最后再进行一次审讯，会进一步影响我们的决定。

column5: You'd have me interrogate the prisoner once more?\nIf I may be so bold — to what end do you request this?
column6: 您要我再审那囚犯一次？\n恕我斗胆——请问您意欲何为？

column5: Not you, Sovy.\nWe want your {i}Apprentice{/i} to do this.\nIt is time for him to prove his worth.
column6: 不是你去，索维。\n我们要你的{i}学徒{/i}去做这件事。\n是时候让他证明自己的价值了。

column5: Their voices echoed loudly through their darkened chambers.{w}\nIt mattered not which Triumvir spoke, for they were all of one mind.{w}\nWith a clear irritation in his voice, Sovy did his best to stay calm.
column6: 他们的声音在昏暗的殿堂里回荡。{w}\n无论开口的是哪位执政官都无所谓，因为他们同心一体。{w}\n索维的声音里透着明显的恼怒，却尽力保持镇定。

column5: My Apprentice...?\nI've told you many times, I want to work alone.\nIt would be more efficient for me to do this myself!
column6: 我的学徒……？\n我已经说过很多次了，我想独自行动。\n我一个人来做会高效得多！

column5: Insubordination...?\nThis is unbecoming of you, Sovy.\nWe demand that you obey.
column6: 抗命……？\n这不是你该有的样子，索维。\n我们命令你服从。

column5: The role of Grand Inquisitor can be very dangerous.\nIf we were to lose you, a replacement would be necessary.\nYou must train this replacement while you still breathe.
column6: 大审判官这个职位可能非常危险。\n万一我们失去了你，就必须有人接替。\n你必须趁还活着的时候培养这个接班人。

column5: As you command.
column6: 遵命。

column5: Sovy turned his back to The Triumvirate and spotted his Apprentice.{w}\nHe was standing by the door, listening to their conversation.{w}\nIf he'd heard of Sovy's distaste for him, he showed no concern.
column6: 索维背过身离开三人执政团，目光落在他的学徒身上。{w}\n那学徒正站在门边，听着他们的谈话。{w}\n即便他听到了索维对他的厌恶，也没有表现出任何在意。

column5: Interrogation, hmm?\nAnd what would you have me extract?\nI thought the prisoner was at his wit's end.
column6: 审讯，嗯？\n那您想让我从他嘴里撬出什么？\n我以为那囚犯已经山穷水尽了。

column5: Anything to confirm our suspicions about Valinorth.\nIf you fail, I will not hesitate to punish you.\nRemember what we're on the verge of.
column6: 任何能证实我们对瓦利诺斯怀疑的东西。\n要是你失败了，我会毫不犹豫地惩罚你。\n记住我们即将成就什么。

column5: I understand, Master.\nI'll do my best to get you what you need.\nWhat are the limits when it comes to my approach?
column6: 我明白，师父。\n我会尽力弄到您需要的东西。\n在手段上，我的底线是什么？

column5: Keep him alive, Halin.\nI find that psychological pain is the most valid approach.\nHe cares more for his Rebel Allies than he does for himself.
column6: 让他活着，哈林。\n我发现精神上的折磨才是最有效的手段。\n他关心反抗军的同伴，胜过关心自己。

column5: Then I will threaten The Rebellion's very core.\nI'm grateful to have this opportunity, Master.\nThings are starting to line up well for me.
column6: 那我就去威胁反抗军的命脉。\n我很感激能有这样的机会，师父。\n局势开始对我有利了。

column5: They tend to do that when you have The Triumvirate's blessing.\nWe should take care of this immediately, and catch them unprepared.\nEvery moment we waste — is a moment they gain, Halin.
column6: 有三人执政团的庇佑，事情往往就会如此。\n我们应当立刻行动，趁他们毫无防备。\n我们浪费的每一刻——都是他们赢得的一刻，哈林。

column5: They leave the room together, talking amongst themselves.{w}\nThe Triumvirate waits until they're gone before speaking.{w}\nA faint smile on their faces, as age-old plans come to fruition.
column6: 他们一同离开房间，边走边低声交谈。{w}\n三人执政团一直等到他们走远，才开口说话。{w}\n他们脸上浮现出一丝浅笑，因为筹划已久的计划即将实现。

column5: So it's finally going to happen, isn't it?\nWhat we've been waiting for, all these years.\nDo you think we should tell Sovy our true plan?
column6: 那么，终于要发生了，是吗？\n我们这些年来一直在等待的事。\n你觉得我们该把真正的计划告诉索维吗？

column5: Halin entered the prison cell, without Sovy at his side.{w}\nHis Master remained outside as a pseudo-display of trust.{w}\nBut it was evident to Halin that no trust existed.
column6: 哈林走进牢房，索维没有跟在他身旁。{w}\n他的师父留在外面，装出信任他的样子。{w}\n但哈林心里清楚，根本不存在什么信任。

column5: The prisoner looked up, surprised to see a different face.{w}\nYet within him, was still a slowly dwindling hope.{w}\nCut off from The Rebellion, these would be his final days.
column6: 囚犯抬起头，看到一张陌生的脸，有些意外。{w}\n然而在他心中，仍残存着一丝慢慢熄灭的希望。{w}\n与反抗军断了联系，这将是他的最后日子。

column5: So someone different has finally come...?\nWhat are you, the executioner or something?\nI figured it was only a matter of time.
column6: 所以终于换了个生面孔来……？\n你是什么人，刽子手之类的？\n我早就料到，这只是时间问题。

column5: Actually, Sovy said to keep you alive.\nYou seem to underestimate your value, Shane.
column6: 其实，索维说要留你一条命。\n你似乎低估了自己的价值，肖恩。

column5: You think I'm important...?\nThat's not what I expected to hear.
column6: 你觉得我重要……？\n这可不在我的意料之中。

column5: Don't take it the wrong way.\nYou must not know what I meant.
column6: 别误会了。\n你肯定没明白我的意思。

column5: He knelt down in front of the prisoner.{w}\nWith a sinister smirk, he tried to intimidate Shane.
column6: 他在囚犯面前蹲下身。{w}\n带着一抹阴森的冷笑，他试图恐吓肖恩。

column5: You're important as a bargaining chip.\nAnd the fact I must keep you alive — is a curse.\nWhen I'm through with you, you'll beg for death.
column6: 你的重要性只是作为筹码。\n而我必须留你活命——这简直是诅咒。\n等我把你收拾完，你会求着去死。

column5: You see, I'm different from Sovy.\nHe's passed the bar — they no longer need to test him.\nBut I'm in the position where results must happen.
column6: 你看，我和索维不一样。\n他已经通过了考验——他们不再需要测试他。\n可我的处境，是必须拿出成果。

column5: When we give you back — you'll be a broken man.\nAnd soon after, the foundation of The Rebellion will crumble. \nYou think we don't know that Damek is your leader?
column6: 等我们把你放回去——你就会是个废人。\n再过不久，反抗军的根基就会崩塌。\n你以为我们不知道达梅克是你们的首领？

column5: What...!?
Shane's eyes shot wide open, in utter shock.{w}\nIt seems that Halin's threats worked to great effect.
column6: 肖恩的双眼猛地瞪大，惊骇万分。{w}\n看来哈林的威胁效果显著。

column5: You'd be stupid not to think we have inside men.\nI could order Damek's execution in a matter of seconds.\nYou don't value your life — but you value his.
column6: 你要是以为我们没有内应，那就太蠢了。\n我可以在几秒之内下令处决达梅克。\n你不看重自己的命——却很看重他的。

column5: Good — now I expect you to answer my questions.\nThe Blade of Exodus, is it in Valinorth Village?\nAnd the one who can wield it, do they live there as well?
column6: 很好——现在，我希望你如实回答我的问题。\n流亡之刃，是不是在瓦利诺斯村？\n还有那个能驾驭它的人，是不是也住在那儿？

column5: By the time we catch up with Ulric, it's already too late.{w}\nHis large blade is in deadlock with one of the enemy soldiers.{w}\nValessa draws her daggers, and I hold out my sword, ready.
column6: 等我们追上乌尔里克时，已经太迟了。{w}\n他的巨剑正与一名敌兵僵持不下。{w}\n瓦莱莎拔出匕首，我也举起剑，严阵以待。

column5: We order you to cease your resistance!\nThose who support The Rebellion must perish!
column6: 我们命令你们停止抵抗！\n拥护反抗军的人都得死！

column5: To break the deadlock, Ulric kicks his opponent in the gut.{w}\nThey stumble back, and ready their blade with a flourish.{w}\nIt isn't much longer until they charge toward him again.
column6: 为了打破僵局，乌尔里克一脚踹在对手的腹部。{w}\n那人踉跄着后退，炫技般重新举起兵器。{w}\n没过多久，他们又朝他冲了过来。

column5: Valessa, your dagger!
column6: 瓦莱莎，你的匕首！

column5: Ulric jumps out of the way, and rolls toward us.{w}\nLanding on his knees, he pries one of the daggers from her grip.{w}\nWithout even looking, he throws it behind himself.
column6: 乌尔里克闪身跃开，朝我们这边翻滚过来。{w}\n他双膝着地，从瓦莱莎手中掰下一把匕首。{w}\n他连看都不看，就把它朝身后扔了出去。

column5: He closes his eyes and looks down at the ground.{w}\nWhen he hears the impact of the dagger, his ears fold back.{w}\nFor a moment, it looks like he's actually sad.
column6: 他闭上眼，低头看着地面。{w}\n听到匕首命中的声音，他的耳朵向后耷拉下去。{w}\n有那么一瞬间，他看起来竟真的有些悲伤。

column5: Spirits, please forgive my misdeeds.\nI acted only to protect those under my watch.
column6: 灵啊，请宽恕我的罪过。\n我这么做，只是为了保护受我守护的人。

column5: Ulric cares about the spirits? For some reason, I didn't expect that.{w}\nBut before I can think about this further, something happens.{w}\nCatching Valessa and I off guard, we're in complete disbelief.
column6: 乌尔里克竟然在意灵？不知为何，我没想到会这样。{w}\n可还没等我细想，意外就发生了。{w}\n我和瓦莱莎猝不及防，简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。

column5: Huh...?
He notices the shocked expression on both of our faces.{w}\nRising to his feet, it's not long before he wears the same look.{w}\nThe enemy soldier fell, as expected, but there was nothing inside.
column6: 他察觉到我们俩脸上震惊的神情。{w}\n等他站起身，脸上很快也露出了同样的表情。{w}\n那名敌兵如预料般倒下，可里面却空无一物。

column5: Scattered pieces of armor litter the ground.{w}\nAs we process this revelation, confusion soon assails us.{w}\nThis was no ordinary attack. What we just saw was {i}impossible{/i}.
column6: 散落的盔甲碎片铺了一地。{w}\n我们消化着这个惊人的事实，困惑随即涌上心头。{w}\n这绝非寻常的袭击。我们刚刚所见，是{i}不可能{/i}发生的。

column5: What's going on...?\nUlric, what are those things!?
column6: 这是怎么回事……？\n乌尔里克，那些东西到底是什么！？

column5: I — I don't know!\nCome closer you two, this doesn't feel right.\nEmpty suits of armor with a hatred for The Rebellion?
column6: 我——我不知道！\n你们俩靠近点，这感觉不对劲。\n空荡荡的盔甲，却对反抗军恨之入骨？

column5: Only those who've mastered the spirits could do this.\nI'm afraid this is much larger than we thought.
column6: 只有掌控了灵的人才能做到这种事。\n恐怕这远比我们想象的要严重得多。

column5: But that can't be true.\nThe spirits are pure, they {i}aid{/i} us.
column6: 但这不可能。\n灵是纯洁的，它们{i}帮助{/i}我们。

column5: Yeah, sure looks like they wanted to help!\nThat's not my only concern though. Look at this.
column6: 是啊，看起来还真像是来帮忙的！\n不过这不是我唯一的顾虑。看这个。

column5: She scoffs as she steps toward the helmet.{w}\nKneeling down, she pulls her dagger out of it.
column6: 她嗤笑一声，朝那头盔走去。{w}\n她蹲下身，把匕首从里面拔了出来。

column5: Do you recognize these colors, Ulric...?
column6: 你认得这些颜色吗，乌尔里克……？

column5: No, why would I—
column6: 不认得，我怎么会——

column5: Gold and White — The Triumvirate's Standard.\nI would have never made such a deduction, but...\nOnly they could wield the spirits in this fashion.
column6: 金色与白色——三人执政团的旗号。\n我本绝不会做出这样的推断，可是……\n只有他们才能以这种方式御使灵。

column5: Our supposed protectors.\nTo some, even the creators of Alestia.\nI have no idea why they'd want to do this to us.
column6: 我们所谓的守护者。\n在某些人眼中，甚至是阿莱斯蒂亚的创造者。\n我真不明白他们为何要这样对待我们。

column5: That's what I'd like to know.\nThey're supposed to be our protectors.\nSome people even think they created Alestia.
column6: 这正是我想弄明白的。\n他们本应是我们的守护者。\n有些人甚至认为他们创造了阿莱斯蒂亚。

column5: Wouldn't be the first time they attempted \"occupation\".\nThey hinted that The Rebellion was involved here?\nValessa, do you know anything about that...?
column6: 这也不是他们第一次试图“占领”了。\n他们暗示反抗军也牵连其中？\n瓦莱莎，这事你知道些什么吗……？

column5: I don't. So much has changed lately.\nWith our last Elder gone, Mylus has been in charge.\nMaybe he has something to tell us...
column6: 我不知道。最近变化太多了。\n上一任长老失踪后，一直是迈勒斯主事。\n也许他能告诉我们些什么……

column5: It's worth a shot, we should see if he's alive.\nProtecting you is my goal, but now I want answers.\nIf anyone knows about this, it would be him.
column6: 值得一试，我们该去看看他还活着没。\n保护你是我的目标，但现在我想要答案。\n若有人知道内情，那一定是他。

column5: To the Elder's house, then?
column6: 那就去长老的家？

column5: Yeah.
column6: 好。

column5: I follow after Valessa and Ulric.{w}\nWe walk along the circular road surrounding the water tank.{w}\nI make note of it for later, it might help put out the flames.
column6: 我跟着瓦莱莎和乌尔里克走。{w}\n我们沿着环绕蓄水池的环形道路前行。{w}\n我把它记在心里，说不定之后能用来灭火。

column5: More suits of armor litter the ground, there's so many of them.{w}\nIt makes me feel a bit hopeful, like we stood a chance.{w}\nThe village wasn't defenseless, and this was proof.
column6: 地上散落着更多盔甲，数量多得惊人。{w}\n这让我稍稍燃起希望，仿佛我们还有胜算。{w}\n村子并非毫无防备，这就是明证。

column5: Aren't you glad we waited, now?\nIf we rushed in head-first, we'd be dead.
column6: 现在你该庆幸我们等了吧？\n要是我们一头冲出去，早就没命了。

column5: Then where are the villagers' bodies?\nI only see the suits of armor lying around.
column6: 那村民们的尸体在哪儿？\n我只看到散落一地的盔甲。

column5: That was a good question, actually.{w}\nNo blood, no signs of a major struggle.{w}\nOnly the fire, and the glistening of the white armor.
column6: 这问题问得好。{w}\n没有血迹，没有激烈搏斗的痕迹。{w}\n只有火焰，和白色盔甲的反光。

column5: That's a good sign.\nThen they won, and fled to safety.\nAre there any havens in Valinorth?
column6: 那是个好兆头。\n这么说他们赢了，逃到安全的地方去了。\n瓦利诺斯有什么避难的地方吗？

column5: I'd say The Elder's house, and The Grand Tree.\nThe fire may not have reached either, yet.
column6: 我想是长老的家，还有巨树。\n大火也许还没烧到这两处。

column5: Wait, how many people can fit in The Grand Tree?
column6: 等等，巨树里能容纳多少人？

column5: Hundreds, easily.
column6: 几百人，轻而易举。

column5: Not as good of a sign as I thought.\nThe enemy could be trying to round everyone up.\nPut them all in one place before killing them.
column6: 这兆头没我想的那么好。\n敌人可能正想把所有人赶拢到一起。\n在杀掉他们之前，先把他们集中到一处。

column5: That's dirty...!
column6: 真卑鄙……！

column5: But it works.\nWe still don't know what they're after.\nIt can't be genocide, it must be something else.
column6: 可这招管用。\n我们仍不知道他们图的是什么。\n不可能是种族灭绝，一定另有目的。

column5: Does Valinorth have anything The Triumvirate would want?\nDid the change in leadership bring anything with it?
column6: 瓦利诺斯有什么是三人执政团想要的吗？\n这次权力更迭有没有带来什么变化？

column5: Like I said, we'd have to talk to Mylus.\nBut I doubt he'd be at The Grand Tree.
column6: 我说过了，得去问迈勒斯。\n不过我猜他不在巨树那儿。

column5: They look at each other, and then look at me.{w}\nI could tell that Valessa was pushing us toward Mylus.{w}\nBut that's because she knew this was a vision.
column6: 他们互相看了看，然后又看向我。{w}\n我看得出瓦莱莎在把我们往迈勒斯那边引。{w}\n那是因为她知道这是一场幻象。

column5: But what if there {i}are{/i} people in The Grand Tree?\nIs Mylus more important than all of them?\nIt would be cold to let everyone die.
column6: 可要是巨树里{i}真的{/i}有人呢？\n迈勒斯比他们所有人都重要吗？\n任由所有人去死，未免太冷酷了。

column5: Ulric, this is larger than Valinorth!\nEspecially if it involves The Rebellion.\nInformation could save entire villages!
column6: 乌尔里克，这件事比瓦利诺斯更大！\n尤其如果牵扯到反抗军。\n情报能救下整个整个的村庄！

column5: I don't like what you're suggesting.
column6: 我不喜欢你话里的意思。

column5: Like it's any better than what you suggested!\nUsing the people as pawns to buy us time.\nHow is this any different!?
column6: 好像你提的就有多高明似的！\n拿人民当棋子换取时间。\n这又有什么不同！？

column5: They fume at each other, but realize it's a stupid argument.{w}\nIn the midst of this battle, nothing was so black-and-white.{w}\nThough I find it odd that Ulric switched viewpoints so fast.
column6: 他们互相生着闷气，但也都意识到这争论毫无意义。{w}\n在这场战乱之中，没有什么事是非黑即白的。{w}\n不过我觉得奇怪，乌尔里克怎么这么快就转变了立场。

column5: This is a matter of Valinorth's future.\nSuch things are under the jurisdiction of the Seer.\nI stand by his side, and you stand by both of ours.
column6: 这关乎瓦利诺斯的未来。\n这类事情归先知管辖。\n我站在他这边，而你站在我们两人这边。

column5: That is, unless you want to abandon your job.\nBut that wouldn't look good on your perfect record.
column6: 当然，除非你想撂挑子不干。\n可那会有损你完美的履历。

column5: This is a matter of Valinorth's future.\nSuch things are under the jurisdiction of the Seeress.\nI stand by her side, and you stand by both of ours.
column6: 这关乎瓦利诺斯的未来。\n这类事情归先知管辖。\n我站在她这边，而你站在我们两人这边。

column5: That is, unless you want to abandon your job.\nBut that wouldn't look good on your perfect record.
column6: 当然，除非你想撂挑子不干。\n可那会有损你完美的履历。

column5: Hmph — I guess you can fight dirty, too.\nI don't like this, but you have me by the throat.\nI can only hope that you make the right choice.
column6: 哼——看来你也懂得使阴招。\n我不喜欢这样，但你掐住了我的命门。\n我只能指望你做出正确的选择。

column5: He stares at me with a serious look on his face.{w}\nTalk about putting me on the spot.{w}\nBut if this was my role, I had to fill the shoes.
column6: 他一脸严肃地盯着我。{w}\n真是把我架在火上烤。{w}\n可如果这就是我的角色，我就必须担起来。

column5: What are we going to do...?
column6: 我们该怎么办……？

column5: Vision or not, I couldn't let all those people die.{w}\nIt was my duty to save as many people as possible.
column6: 不管是不是幻象，我都不能眼看着那些人去死。{w}\n尽可能多救人，是我的职责。

column5: Good to know we're on the same page.\nMylus can't be the only one with information.
column6: 很高兴我们想法一致。\n掌握情报的人不可能只有迈勒斯一个。

column5: Are you sure about this!?\nRemember what we talked about.
column6: 你确定要这样吗！？\n别忘了我们谈过的。

column5: I nodded, and reiterated my stance on the matter.{w}\nNothing was more important than saving innocent lives.{w}\nAll the better if some of them had important information.
column6: 我点了点头，重申了我在此事上的立场。{w}\n没有什么比拯救无辜者的性命更重要。{w}\n如果他们中有人掌握重要情报，那就更好了。

column5: We change our course and head to The Grand Tree.{w}\nIt didn't feel good to abandon Mylus, but we had to.{w}\nThis was real. I'd use the future to cheat the present.
column6: 我们改变路线，朝巨树而去。{w}\n抛下迈勒斯让人心里不好受，但我们别无选择。{w}\n这是真实的。我要用未来去欺骗当下。

column5: I vowed to stop this attack, and I needed information.{w}\nIf anybody could give us that information, it would be Mylus.{w}\nHe'd be able to shed light on The Rebellion's involvement, too.
column6: 我发誓要阻止这场袭击，而我需要情报。{w}\n若有人能给我们情报，那一定是迈勒斯。{w}\n他也能为我们揭开反抗军牵涉其中的内情。

column5: Good, we're on the same page.\nWe can use that information to help others.\nIt would be selfish to focus only on Valinorth.
column6: 很好，我们想到一块儿去了。\n我们可以用这些情报去帮助其他人。\n只盯着瓦利诺斯，那就太自私了。

column5: I hope you two are certain about this!\nYou're gambling with hundreds of lives!
column6: 但愿你们俩确定要这么做！\n你们是在拿几百条人命赌博！

column5: Ulric didn't understand this like we did.{w}\nAnd we weren't about to waste time lecturing him.{w}\nI was grateful that his job required following us.
column6: 乌尔里克不像我们这样明白其中缘由。{w}\n而我们也不打算浪费时间跟他讲道理。{w}\n我反倒庆幸，他的职责要求他必须跟着我们。

column5: We continued in the same direction, heading to Mylus' house.{w}\nIt didn't feel good to abandon others, but we had to do it.{w}\nThis was real. I'd use the future to cheat the present.
column6: 我们继续沿原方向前行，朝迈勒斯的家走去。{w}\n抛下别人让人心里不好受，但我们不得不这么做。{w}\n这是真实的。我要用未来去欺骗当下。

column5: In the present day, Damek found himself lost in thought.{w}\nUsing the tunnels under Mazeo for solitude, he found peace.{w}\nThere was much to plan, but for once, they had the upper hand.
column6: 而在当下，达梅克陷入了沉思。{w}\n他借马泽奥城下的隧道独处，寻得一片安宁。{w}\n有许多事要谋划，但这一次，他们占了上风。

column5: Valinorth... The Blade of Exodus...\nThere must be something the spirits aren't telling us.\nSomething we could use to take down The Triumvirate.
column6: 瓦利诺斯……流亡之刃……\n灵一定还有什么没告诉我们。\n某种我们能用来了结三人执政团的东西。

column5: When I touched the blade, I saw our victory.\nBut I'm not trained to interpret such things.\nI pray for the cooperation of Valinorth...
column6: 我触到那把剑时，看到了我们的胜利。\n但我不懂得如何解读这类事物。\n我祈求瓦利诺斯愿意合作……

column5: One of his advisors approaches, careful not to startle him.{w}\nWhen he realizes he's detected, he lets out a soft yawn.
column6: 他的一名顾问走过来，小心翼翼地不惊扰他。{w}\n当他意识到自己已被察觉，便轻轻打了个哈欠。

column5: Another one of those sleepless nights, Damek?\nI can't blame you. It's been the same with me.\nDid I hear you say something about Valinorth...?
column6: 又是一个不眠之夜吗，达梅克？\n这怪不得你。我也一样。\n我是不是听到你提到瓦利诺斯……？

column5: Yeah, I was thinking out loud.\nIn Valinorth, there's a person who can peer into the future.\nThat's why I had Pro bring the blade there last week.
column6: 是啊，我自言自语罢了。\n瓦利诺斯有个人能窥见未来。\n所以上周我才让普洛把剑送到那里去。

column5: I'm aware of their culture.\nBut their Seers use spirits, not a blade.\nDo you think it will be that easy?
column6: 我对他们的文化有所了解。\n但他们的先知用的是灵，不是剑。\n你觉得会那么容易吗？

column5: Worth the gamble, isn't it?\nIt's not my place to wield knowledge of the future.\nBut The Seers are experts. Conditioned from birth.
column6: 值得一赌，不是吗？\n驾驭未来的知识不是我的本分。\n但先知们是行家，自出生起便受训。

column5: Pro has sent word that the current Seer is male.\nHis investigation is progressing slower than I'd like.\nWe need to pick up the pace, and fast.
column6: 普洛传信说，现任先知是男性。\n他的调查进展比我期望的要慢。\n我们得加快节奏，而且要快。

column5: Pro has sent word that the current Seer is female.\nHis investigation is progressing slower than I'd like.\nWe need to pick up the pace, and fast.
column6: 普洛传信说，现任先知是女性。\n他的调查进展比我期望的要慢。\n我们得加快节奏，而且要快。

column5: Now that they have the blade, they're a target.\nThe Triumvirate is likely planning their attack as we speak.\nThat's why I've decided to send an experienced fighter.
column6: 既然他们拿到了剑，就成了目标。\n很可能我们说话这会儿，三人执政团正在筹划进攻。\n所以我才决定派一名经验丰富的战士过去。

column5: I guess that's me.
column6: 我想就是我吧。

column5: I've had the Mayor of Mazeo write up a decree.\nIt will allow you entry, and the ability to complete what Pro started.\nOn paper, and to everyone else, it's a simple export.
column6: 我让马泽奥的市长拟了一道法令。\n它能让你入境，并接手完成普洛未竟的事。\n从文件和旁人看来，这只是一桩普通的出口生意。

column5: Only Mylus knows the importance of this blade.\nAll you have to do is deliver it from Valinorth, back to me.\nThat is, with the Seer at your side, Ulric.
column6: 只有迈勒斯知道这把剑的分量。\n你只需把它从瓦利诺斯送回我手里。\n当然，还要把先知也带在你身边，乌尔里克。

column5: You seem to think that will be easy.\nIt's not likely they know the truth of Valinorth.\nI can bring the Seer, but they'll just decline.
column6: 你似乎觉得这事很容易。\n他们多半并不知道瓦利诺斯的真相。\n我可以把先知带来，但他们只会拒绝。

column5: Only Mylus knows the importance of this blade.\nAll you have to do is deliver it from Valinorth, back to me.\nThat is, with the Seeress at your side, Ulric.
column6: 只有迈勒斯知道这把剑的分量。\n你只需把它从瓦利诺斯送回我手里。\n当然，还要把先知也带在你身边，乌尔里克。

column5: You seem to think that will be easy.\nIt's not likely they know the truth of Valinorth.\nI can bring the Seeress, but they'll just decline.
column6: 你似乎觉得这事很容易。\n他们多半并不知道瓦利诺斯的真相。\n我可以把先知带来，但他们只会拒绝。

column5: Present yourself as a mercenary, not a Rebel.\nTell them a meeting of importance is happening in Mazeo.\nWe want their ability to help with some \"important decisions\".
column6: 你要以雇佣兵的身份现身，而不是反抗军。\n告诉他们马泽奥正开一场重要的会议。\n我们想要借助他们的能力，来协助一些“重要决策”。

column5: Dishonesty?\nGreat way to start a partnership.
column6: 靠欺骗？\n这可真是开启合作的好方式啊。

column5: It worked for us, don't you remember?\nLook at how invaluable you've become.
column6: 这招对我们管用，你不记得了吗？\n看看你现在变得多不可或缺。

column5: Ulric laughed and turned to look at the dark depths of the tunnels.{w}\nAt the moment, everything ahead seemed bleak and uncertain.{w}\nHaving an ally cast light on that future would be a tremendous boon.
column6: 乌尔里克笑了笑，转头望向隧道幽深的黑暗。{w}\n此刻，前路显得黯淡而莫测。{w}\n若能有一位盟友为那未来照亮道路，将是巨大的助力。

column5: So this is it, isn't it?\nWith the Seer at our side, they can direct us.\nWe can secure the victory that you witnessed.
column6: 那么，就是这么回事了，对吧？\n有先知站在我们这边，就能为我们指引方向。\n我们能稳操你所见的那场胜局。

column5: So this is it, isn't it?\nWith the Seeress at our side, they can direct us.\nWe can secure the victory that you witnessed.
column6: 那么，就是这么回事了，对吧？\n有先知站在我们这边，就能为我们指引方向。\n我们能稳操你所见的那场胜局。

column5: I almost don't believe it, but it's true.\nThough I have to be honest with you Ulric.\nThere's a reason why I'm sending you instead of asking Pro.
column6: 我几乎不敢相信，但这是真的。\n不过我得跟你说实话，乌尔里克。\n我派你去而不是找普洛，是有原因的。

column5: And what's that?
column6: 什么原因？

column5: He may not be strong enough to face what's coming.\nIt's not just a hunch that Valinorth will be attacked.\nIn our victory, I saw its death and destruction.
column6: 他或许不够强，无法面对即将到来的一切。\n瓦利诺斯会遭袭，这不只是我的直觉。\n在那场胜利中，我看到了它的毁灭与死亡。

column5: I see.
column6: 我明白了。

column5: So I ask that you protect the Seer and his allies at all costs.\nAnd when you come across Pro, have him join you as well.\nI'll make sure to prepare an exquisite welcoming party.
column6: 所以我请求你，不惜一切代价保护先知和他的盟友。\n等你遇见普洛时，也让他加入你们。\n我一定会备下一场盛大的接风宴。

column5: So I ask that you protect the Seeress and her allies at all costs.\nAnd when you come across Pro, have him join you as well.\nI'll make sure to prepare an exquisite welcoming party.
column6: 所以我请求你，不惜一切代价保护先知和她的盟友。\n等你遇见普洛时，也让他加入你们。\n我一定会备下一场盛大的接风宴。

column5: I'll leave first thing in the morning.\nWhat did you see, exactly?
column6: 我一早就出发。\n你到底看到了什么？

column5: Nothing you can't fight your way out of.\nBut trust me, it will show them the truth.\nAnd when you get back, they'll be ready to fight.
column6: 不是那种你杀不出去的困境。\n但相信我，这会让他们看清真相。\n等你回来时，他们就会准备好战斗。

column5: But promise me one thing, and one thing only.\nThat along the way, the Seer touches the blade.\nIf he can wield it, then we have our greatest weapon.
column6: 但你要答应我一件事，仅此一件。\n在路上，让先知触碰那把剑。\n如果他驾驭得了它，我们就有了最强大的武器。

column5: But promise me one thing, and one thing only.\nThat along the way, the Seeress touches the blade.\nIf she can wield it, then we have our greatest weapon.
column6: 但你要答应我一件事，仅此一件。\n在路上，让先知触碰那把剑。\n如果她驾驭得了它，我们就有了最强大的武器。

column5: We enter The Grand Tree, thankful that it's not ablaze.{w}\nBut something else immediately stands out. It's empty.{w}\nThe survivors that we hoped to see were nowhere to be found.
column6: 我们走进巨树，庆幸它还没有起火。{w}\n但另一样东西立刻映入眼帘。这里空无一人。{w}\n我们盼着见到的幸存者，踪影全无。

column5: Empty, huh...?\nJust what the hell is going on, here?
column6: 空的，是吗……？\n这里到底他妈的发生什么了？

column5: I can't believe what I'm seeing right now.\nWhere are all the villagers...?\nThere must be something here!
column6: 我简直不敢相信眼前的景象。\n村民们都去哪儿了……？\n这里一定有什么线索！

column5: Something like what...?
column6: 什么线索……？

column5: Ulric, The Triumvirate is burning down Valinorth!\nThey seem to think we're caught up with The Rebels.\nThinking there's no evidence? That's stupid!
column6: 乌尔里克，三人执政团正在烧毁瓦利诺斯！\n他们似乎以为我们和反抗军是一伙的。\n以为这里没有证据？真是愚蠢！

column5: She starts pacing around The Grand Tree, mumbling.{w}\nI can tell she's searching for something, but I don't know what.{w}\nI look at Ulric, and he shrugs, just as uncertain as me.
column6: 她开始在巨树里来回踱步，嘴里喃喃自语。{w}\n我看得出她在找什么，却不知道是什么。{w}\n我看向乌尔里克，他耸耸肩，和我一样茫然。

column5: Look, maybe Mylus knew we'd come here!\nHe must've left something behind for us, right?\nThere's no survivors here, so we're back to evidence now.
column6: 你看，也许迈勒斯早就知道我们会来这儿！\n他一定给我们留了什么东西，对吧？\n这里没有幸存者，所以现在又得靠找证据了。

column5: Ulric sighs and starts looking around as well.{w}\nWhatever it is that Valessa wants to find, hopefully it's here.
column6: 乌尔里克叹了口气，也开始四下查看。{w}\n不管瓦莱莎想找的是什么，但愿它就在这儿。

column5: None of this is helping, Valessa!\nIt's a tree. Nothing more, nothing less.
column6: 这些都没用，瓦莱莎！\n它就是一棵树。仅此而已。

column5: No, there has to be something here!\nCome on Seer, give us a hand!
column6: 不，这里一定有什么东西！\n来吧，先知，帮我们一把！

column5: No, there must be something here!\nCome on Seeress, give us a hand!
column6: 不，这里一定有什么东西！\n来吧，先知，帮我们一把！

column5: It is optional, but highly recommended that you talk to your comrades.
column6: 与同伴交谈是可选的，但强烈建议这么做。

column5: Hmm?
column6: 嗯？

column5: I wish. This whole place is a mess.\nHonestly, I don't even know what to look for.\nMylus isn't stupid though. He'd leave {i}something{/i}.
column6: 我倒希望如此。这地方一团糟。\n说实话，我连该找什么都不知道。\n不过迈勒斯不傻。他一定会留下{i}什么{/i}。

column5: Honestly, only a few months.\nHe was thrust into the position against his will.\nSomething happened to his Father, the previous Elder.
column6: 说实话，才几个月。\n他是被迫坐上这个位置的。\n他父亲，也就是上一任长老，出了事。

column5: But he's done such a good job, it's crazy.\nThe leadership of Valinorth did {i}not{/i} skip a beat!\nHe must've been training under his Father.
column6: 可他做得非常好，简直让人难以置信。\n瓦利诺斯的领导层{i}丝毫{/i}没有出现断层！\n他一定一直在父亲手下受训。

column5: Nobody knows, actually.\nHe went on a trip to Mazeo and never came back.\nSearch parties came up with nothing, it's like he vanished.
column6: 其实没人知道。\n他去马泽奥一趟，就再也没回来。\n搜索队一无所获，他就这样凭空消失了。

column5: Normally we'd hold an election, but things were crazy.\nThat, and Valinorth is really big on \"family\" and \"tradition\".\nEveryone just seemed to expect that Mylus would take over.
column6: 按惯例我们该举行选举，可当时局面太乱。\n再加上瓦利诺斯格外看重“家族”与“传统”。\n大家似乎都认定迈勒斯会继任。

column5: Sorry, I guess you're right.\nI'm not really treating this as \"real\".\nIt's something you learn to do early on.
column6: 抱歉，我想你说得对。\n我确实没把这一切当成“真的”。\n这是你从小就得学会的事。

column5: But this seems premeditated, to say the least.\nThe Triumvirate must've been planning this for a while.\nMylus taking over? I doubt that's directly related.
column6: 但至少可以说，这一切像是早有预谋。\n三人执政团一定谋划了许久。\n迈勒斯继任？我怀疑那没有直接关系。

column5: He's performed admirably for the position he's in.\nI doubt even a full election would find a better candidate.\nI was scared for a while, but he really filled the role.
column6: 以他的处境而言，他表现得相当出色。\n我怀疑就算举行完整的选举，也找不到更好的人选。\n我曾担心过一阵，但他确实胜任了这个角色。

column5: He didn't want to do it, but he kind of had to.\nIt all happened so fast, I'm not sure of the specifics.\nBut it was seamless, you almost couldn't notice.
column6: 他并不想这么做，但又不得不如此。\n一切都发生得太快，我不清楚细节。\n但过渡得毫无破绽，你几乎察觉不到。

column5: I guess, but we can't all get what we want.\nIt's not like I grew up wanting to be a Scribe.\nHe'll grow into the role, I'm sure of it.
column6: 也许吧，可我们没法都如愿以偿。\n我从小也没想过要当书记官。\n他会慢慢胜任这个角色的，我确信。

column5: But we can worry about that after this is over.\nThere's lots to do, and we can't even find him.\nI really hope that nothing bad has happened.
column6: 但这些等事情结束后再操心吧。\n有太多事要做，我们却连人都找不到。\n我真希望没有出什么坏事。

column5: Wait, you want to be the Elder?\nAre you sure you don't have a full plate right now?\nI mean, we could always try to find someone more willing.
column6: 等等，你想当长老？\n你确定现在你手头不是已经够忙了吗？\n我是说，我们总能找个更愿意的人。

column5: But we can worry about that after this is over.\nThere's lots to do, and we can't even find him.\nI really hope that nothing bad has happened.
column6: 但这些等事情结束后再操心吧。\n有太多事要做，我们却连人都找不到。\n我真希望没有出什么坏事。

column5: I agree, but I feel a bit sorry for him.\nYou can see it in his eyes, it stresses him out.\nMaybe we can find someone more willing, you know?
column6: 我同意，但我有点替他难过。\n从他眼神里就能看出来，这让他压力很大。\n也许我们能找个更愿意的人，你懂的？

column5: But we can worry about that after this is over.\nThere's lots to do, and we can't even find him.\nI really hope that nothing bad has happened.
column6: 但这些等事情结束后再操心吧。\n有太多事要做，我们却连人都找不到。\n我真希望没有出什么坏事。

column5: I'd want to get to the bottom of it, then.\nThere's more going on than we can take at face value.\nHe'd have his reasons, and I'd want to hear all of them.
column6: 那我就想把事情查个水落石出。\n这里面另有隐情，不能只看表面。\n他一定有自己的理由，而我想全部听他说清楚。

column5: That's the thing though, it's not actually happening.\nIf he can explain himself, and we can prevent this...?\nWell, then we can deal with it in a reasonable way.
column6: 可问题就在于，这一切其实并未发生。\n要是他能解释清楚，而我们又能阻止这一切……？\n那好，到时我们就能用理智的方式处理。

column5: We can't condemn him on a vision like this.\nThat's like hating someone for what they do in a dream.\nBesides, we have no way of confirming this is his fault.
column6: 我们不能凭这样一场幻象就给他定罪。\n那就好比因为某人梦里做的事去恨他。\n再说，我们也无从证实这是他的过错。

column5: And it's something I'd happily listen to.\nThat is, after we find a way to prevent this.\nI'm not passing judgement until I hear more.
column6: 而我也乐于听他说。\n前提是，我们先找到阻止这一切的办法。\n在听到更多之前，我不会妄下判断。

column5: We can't condemn him based on a vision like this.\nThat's like hating someone for what they do in a dream.\nBesides, we have no way of confirming this is his fault.
column6: 我们不能凭这样一场幻象就给他定罪。\n那就好比因为某人梦里做的事去恨他。\n再说，我们也无从证实这是他的过错。

column5: I'm making a pretty educated guess.\nI'm trained to detect this kind of stuff.\nBut it's so weird, because this feels like reality.
column6: 我是凭经验做了相当靠谱的推断。\n我受过训练，能察觉这类事物。\n可这太奇怪了，因为这里感觉就像现实。

column5: What's going to happen to me...?\nI mean technically, I'm not real, right?\nThat's hard to take in. This feels real to me.
column6: 我会怎么样呢……？\n我是说，严格来讲，我不是真实的，对吧？\n这很难接受。可对我来说，这一切都无比真实。

column5: But the way you're acting, yeah, it makes me certain.\nIt's very rare that I become lucid in a vision.\nBut with the evidence at hand, I'm very sure.
column6: 但看你的举止，对，这让我确信了。\n我在幻象中保持清醒的时刻极其罕见。\n但就现有证据来看，我非常确定。

column5: Better not talk about it too loud, though.\nWouldn't want Ulric to realize something is up.\nThe rules state that only you and I can know.
column6: 不过，最好别说得太大声。\n可不能让乌尔里克察觉出什么。\n规矩就是，此事只能你我知道。

column5: Trust me, it's better for him not to know.\nHe'd act recklessly, and he'd be really confused.\nWell, more reckless than normal, I mean.
column6: 相信我，他不知道最好。\n他会行事鲁莽，而且会彻底懵掉。\n呃，我是说，比平时更鲁莽。

column5: There's entire books written on this subject, you know.\nBut no one must know when they're in a vision.\nIt could screw up what the spirits want to show us.
column6: 你知道吗，关于这个主题有成书论述。\n但身处幻象中时，绝不能让旁人知道。\n那会搅乱灵想让我们看到的东西。

column5: These are gifts. Blessings, directly from the realm of spirits.\nWe're not in any position to harm what they give us.
column6: 这是恩赐。是来自灵界的祝福。\n我们无权去破坏它们给予我们的东西。

column5: As long as any other dream, I guess.\nOr maybe when the spirits decide you've seen enough.\nThat's one of the things we don't really know.
column6: 我猜，和寻常的梦一样长吧。\n或者，也许直到灵认为你看够了为止。\n这正是我们并不真正了解的事情之一。

column5: I guess something traumatic, like your death, would end it.\nOur minds aren't fit to comprehend what would happen next.\nWe should make the most of the time we {i}do{/i} have in here.
column6: 我猜，某种创伤性的事件，比如你的死亡，会终结它。\n我们的心智无法理解之后会发生什么。\n我们该好好利用在{i}这里{/i}所拥有的时间。

column5: Nobody knows, but we assume it's to protect us.\nIf we know what's coming, we can change what happens.\nSeers have done it time and time again for thousands of years.
column6: 没人知道，但我们猜想是为了保护我们。\n若我们知晓即将发生什么，就能改变结局。\n数千年来，先知们一次又一次做到了这点。

column5: A lot of people think they'll want something in exchange.\nThat they're planting seeds to reap later down the line.\nA stupid superstition if you ask me. They just want to help.
column6: 很多人以为它们会索取回报。\n以为它们在播种，日后好收割。\n要我说，这是愚蠢的迷信。它们只是想帮忙。

column5: Well, I guess we'll have to disagree on that!\nThere's nothing more pure than the spirits.\nThis gift is a truly beautiful thing.
column6: 好吧，看来这点上我们只能保留分歧了！\n没有什么比灵更纯净。\n这份恩赐真是美好至极。

column5: Yeah, I agree!\nThere's nothing more pure than the spirits.\nWithout the visions, we'd have died out ages ago.
column6: 是啊，我同意！\n没有什么比灵更纯净。\n没有这些幻象，我们早就灭绝了。

column5: This particular vision? No.\nBut the concept of visions in general? Yes.\nWithout them, we'd have gone extinct long ago.
column6: 这一场幻象？不算。\n但笼统地说，幻象这个概念本身？算。\n没有它们，我们早就灭绝了。

column5: They guide the world to a better future.\nAnd what's better, they ask for nothing in return.\nOnly that we continue to harness this amazing power.
column6: 它们引导世界走向更美好的未来。\n更难得的是，它们不求任何回报。\n只愿我们继续驾驭这份奇妙的力量。

column5: Yeah, it's just like I said. For better or worse.\nI was trained to be your Scribe from a young age.\nWe've been inseparable ever since.
column6: 是啊，就像我说的。无论好坏。\n我从小就受训做你的书记官。\n从那时起，我们就形影不离。

column5: It's not exactly what I grew up wanting.\nBut I'm not in a position to shun Valinorth's tradition.\nBesides, I could think of people {i}much{/i} worse to serve.
column6: 这并不完全是我从小心中的愿望。\n但我没有资格背弃瓦利诺斯的传统。\n再说，我想得出{i}远比这{/i}更糟的效忠对象。

column5: Actually, you're seeing them firsthand.\nImagine how confused you'd be without me.\nWe're supposed to guide you through these visions.
column6: 其实，你正亲眼见证着这一切。\n想象一下没有我你会有多困惑。\n我们的职责就是引领你走过这些幻象。

column5: But when you wake up, you also need to report to me.\nOr, I guess you can report to Mylus in these dire circumstances.\nEither way, I help you in here, and you report out there.
column6: 但你醒来后，也得向我汇报。\n或者，我想在这种情况下，你也能向迈勒斯汇报。\n总之，我在这里面帮你，你在外面汇报。

column5: If it weren't for me, you wouldn't remember this.\nYou'd wake up, shrug it off, and go about your day.\nImagine what would happen to Valinorth then.
column6: 要是没有我，你根本不会记得这一切。\n你会醒来，耸耸肩，照常过日子。\n想想那样瓦利诺斯会是什么下场。

column5: Of course not! We're two sides of the same coin!\nHonestly, I wouldn't be able to do anything without you.\nA Scribe would do little good without visions to inhabit.
column6: 当然不会！我们就像同一枚硬币的两面！\n说实话，没有你我也什么都做不了。\n没有幻象可供进入，书记官也派不上什么用场。

column5: Whoa, let's all make assumptions!\nI'm going to pretend I didn't hear that.\nWe work as a {i}team{/i}, we both help each other.
column6: 哇哦，大家可都开始妄加揣测了！\n我就当没听见好了。\n我们是{i}团队{/i}，彼此扶持。

column5: You'd be clueless if I didn't chime in earlier.\nI don't downplay your ability, and I expect the same.\nPerhaps you lose both memory {i}and{/i} manners in visions.
column6: 要不是我刚才插话，你还一头雾水呢。\n我没有贬低你的能力，也指望你别这么对我。\n也许你在幻象里连记忆{i}带{/i}礼数都丢了。

column5: Yes and no. Actually it's pretty technical.\nI'm your only Scribe, but there's also a Scribe-in-training.\nHis name is Fortaime, and he's prepared to take over if needed.
column6: 是，也不是。其实这挺讲究的。\n我是你唯一的书记官，但也有一位见习书记官。\n他叫福泰姆，随时准备在需要时接手。

column5: It's a recent addition to the ranks, but it helps out a lot.\nWithout a Scribe, your abilities would be pretty useless.\nHaving someone fully trained means no one misses a beat.
column6: 这是最近才增设的职位，但帮了大忙。\n没有书记官，你的能力几乎毫无用处。\n有一个受过完整训练的人，就意味着不会有任何疏漏。

column5: Imagine if you had this vision while I was gone.\nJust from that, I think you can gauge Fortaime's importance.\nHe's a nice guy too, but I'm sure he's long since fled.
column6: 想象一下，假如我不在时你陷入这场幻象。\n仅凭这一点，我想你就能明白福泰姆的重要性。\n他人也不错，不过我想他早就逃走了。

column5: I'm sure you'll meet him when you get out of here.\nHe tends to knock on your door first thing in the morning.\nSo let's focus on the matter at hand, alright?
column6: 我相信等你从这里出去，就会见到他。\n他总爱一大早就来敲你的门。\n所以咱们先专注眼前的事，好吗？

column5: Since I was a little kid, actually.\nI was trained to be your Scribe from the moment I could speak.\nIt's a prestigious position, and I couldn't exactly say no.
column6: 其实，从我小时候就开始了。\n我刚会说话就被训练做你的书记官。\n这是个光荣的职位，我也没法拒绝。

column5: Some of the other children were jealous.\nTheir parents too, which seemed really immature to me.\nApparently, there's some competition for the role.
column6: 别的孩子里有人嫉妒。\n他们的父母也一样，在我看来真是幼稚得很。\n据说，这个职位还挺有竞争的。

column5: But the Elder chose me, and like it or not, here I am.\nI guess I'm just blessed that I actually {i}do{/i} like this arrangement.\nIn the end, the spirits really were looking down on me.
column6: 但长老选中了我，不管愿不愿意，我就站在这里。\n我只能庆幸自己{i}确实{/i}喜欢这样的安排。\n到头来，灵真的眷顾了我。

column5: Even if being here right now is terrifying, I'm still happy.\nDoing my duty to save Valinorth, it's a dream come true.\nWe don't know if the other kids would've fit this role.
column6: 哪怕此刻身处这里无比可怕，我依然感到幸福。\n履行拯救瓦利诺斯的职责，对我来说是梦想成真。\n我们也不知道别的孩子是否能胜任这个角色。

column5: Well I guess the answer is both yes and no.\nBefore my parents passed on, they took care of the paperwork.\nUntil I came of age, I had no choice but to obey.
column6: 嗯，我想答案既是又不是。\n在我父母过世前，他们办好了那些文书。\n在成年之前，我除了服从别无选择。

column5: When I did come of age, however, I got to choose.\nLeave Valinorth and pursue my own dreams, or be your Scribe.\nI guess it's pretty obvious which one I chose, huh?
column6: 可等我成年后，我有了选择权。\n离开瓦利诺斯去追寻自己的梦想，或者做你的书记官。\n我选了哪个，应该很明显吧，嗯？

column5: So, while I was forced into the role, I chose to stick with it.\nAlthough, if this is any indication, we might have to leave Valinorth.\nIn that case, I'd get to be your scribe, {i}and{/i} travel the world.
column6: 所以，虽然当初是被迫入行，我却选择坚持下来。\n不过，如果眼下这事算是征兆，我们或许得离开瓦利诺斯。\n那样的话，我就能既做你的书记官，{i}又{/i}游历世界了。

column5: Well, we can't stop this attack from happening.\nWe can only take precautions, and mitigate the damage.\nYour life is valuable, so we should move you elsewhere.
column6: 嗯，我们无法阻止这场袭击发生。\n只能提前防范，把损失降到最低。\n你的命很宝贵，我们该把你转移到别处。

column5: And wherever you go, I'm bound to follow.\nWe'd be the first duo to operate outside of Valinorth.\nNever thought we'd actually make history, but here we are.
column6: 无论你去哪里，我都必须跟随。\n我们将是第一对在瓦利诺斯之外活动的搭档。\n从没想过我们真能创造历史，可眼下就是如此。

column5: Yeah, and same to you.\nLook at this vision. We're going to do great things.\nLet's get to the bottom of this, and save our village together!
column6: 是啊，你也一样。\n看看这场幻象。我们会成就一番大业。\n让我们查清真相，一起拯救我们的村庄！

column5: There's some kind of idol here, it's spinning and glowing.{w}\nI've never seen anything like it before. It's beautiful.{w}\nPerhaps it's able to harness the energy of the spirits.
column6: 这里有个类似灵像的东西，正旋转着发光。{w}\n我从没见过这样的东西。真美。{w}\n也许它能汇聚灵的能量。

column5: It's moving perpetually, without any external force.{w}\nI could actually stare at it for hours on end.{w}\nRight now though, there were more important matters at hand.
column6: 它无需任何外力，便永不停歇地转动。{w}\n我真能盯着它看上好几个钟头。{w}\n不过眼下，还有更重要的事要做。

column5: I walk over to the altar in The Grand Tree.{w}\nThere's a book sitting there, its pages spread open.{w}\nAt first glance, it looks completely unimportant.
column6: 我走向巨树中的祭坛。{w}\n那里放着一本书，书页摊开着。{w}\n乍一看，它似乎毫不重要。

column5: But I flip a few pages, and then I realize.{w}\nThere's a small piece of paper hidden between a few pages.{w}\nIt was important enough to hide, so I quickly read the contents.
column6: 但我翻了几页，随即发现了。{w}\n几页之间藏着一小张纸。{w}\n既然重要到要藏起来，我便迅速读了起来。

column5: I walk over to the altar in The Grand Tree.{w}\nThere's a book sitting there, its pages spread open.{w}\nAt first glance, it looks completely unimportant.
column6: 我走向巨树中的祭坛。{w}\n那里放着一本书，书页摊开着。{w}\n乍一看，它似乎毫不重要。

column5: But I flip a few pages, and then I realize.{w}\nThere's a small piece of paper hidden between a few pages.{w}\nIt was important enough to hide, so I quickly read the contents.
column6: 但我翻了几页，随即发现了。{w}\n几页之间藏着一小张纸。{w}\n既然重要到要藏起来，我便迅速读了起来。

column5: There's a spot that looks weak.{w}\nI move some vines aside and find a little alcove.{w}\nPart of me hopes that survivors are hiding down here.
column6: 有处地方看起来不太牢固。{w}\n我拨开一些藤蔓，发现了一个小壁龛。{w}\n我心底有些希望，也许有幸存者躲在这里。

column5: But there are none.{w}\nJust a pile of old dusty books.{w}\nAt the moment, none of them seem relevant.
column6: 可一个人也没有。{w}\n只有一堆积满灰尘的旧书。{w}\n眼下，它们似乎都无关紧要。

column5: The vines underneath the altar are huge.{w}\nThis tree must be thousands of years old.{w}\nI wonder, then, if it predates The Triumvirate?
column6: 祭坛下的藤蔓粗壮无比。{w}\n这棵树一定有几千年的树龄了。{w}\n那么我不禁想，它是否比三人执政团还要古老？

column5: This light isn't from outside.{w}\nThe tree is actually bioluminescent.{w}\nI wonder if the spirit realm is the cause?
column6: 这光并非来自外面。{w}\n这棵树本身竟能发出生物光。{w}\n我不禁猜想，会不会是灵界所致？

column5: This looks like a comfortable place to sit down.{w}\nUnfortunately, I don't think we have the time to relax.{w}\nI better get back to searching with Ulric and Valessa.
column6: 这看起来是个适合坐下的舒服地方。{w}\n可惜，我想我们没时间休息。{w}\n我还是回去和乌尔里克、瓦莱莎一起找吧。

column5: There's a bright light coming from deep within the tree.{w}\nI'm not sure how to explain it, but the tree is glowing.{w}\nThey say that nature is a container for spiritual energy.
column6: 树深处透出一道明亮的光。{w}\n我不知道该怎么解释，但这棵树在发光。{w}\n据说大自然正是灵性力量的容器。

column5: That's why Valinorth is so in tune with the spirit realm.{w}\nBecause it's the only forested area in all of Alestia.{w}\nThe rest of the world has been deforested and settled upon.
column6: 这就是瓦利诺斯与灵界如此契合的原因。{w}\n因为它是整个阿莱斯蒂亚唯一一片森林地带。{w}\n世界其他地方早已被砍伐殆尽，建满了城镇。

column5: Hmm...
No, there's not much here.\nBut I guess if we spread out, we stand a better chance.\nNot that there's too much ground to cover.
column6: 没有，这里没什么东西。\n但我想，如果我们分头找，机会会大些。\n反正也没多大地方要搜。

column5: If I knew, we'd have found it already.\nValessa seems to think Mylus left something behind.\nBut he isn't dumb. He wouldn't leave stuff out in the open.
column6: 我要是知道，早就找到了。\n瓦莱莎似乎认为迈勒斯留下了什么。\n可他不傻。他不会把东西明晃晃地摆在外面。

column5: If it were up to me, we'd all be long gone.\nI can't fight your choice though, it's your village.\nLet's do our best to hurry and get out of here.
column6: 要我拿主意，我们早就走了。\n可我没法反对你们的选择，这是你们的村子。\n咱们尽力快点，然后离开这里。

column5: Actually, I was going to ask you.\nI thought you two were in sync or something.\nDon't think I didn't notice your secret \"talks\".
column6: 其实，我正想问你们呢。\n我还以为你们俩心有灵犀呢。\n别以为我没注意到你们的秘密“谈话”。

column5: But I'm not mad or anything.\nI know the relationship between you, and your culture.\nWhatever it is, it's not like you're plotting against me.
column6: 但我没有生气什么的。\n我了解你们之间的关系，也了解你们的文化。\n不管是什么，你们总不至于在密谋对付我。

column5: Huh? You mean today, or in general?
column6: 嗯？你是说今天，还是一直如此？

column5: Oh, I'm a mercenary from Mazeo.\nI was actually hired to come bring you back there.\nA summit is happening, and they want your input.
column6: 哦，我是来自马泽奥的雇佣兵。\n其实是有人雇我来把你们带回去。\n那里要开一场峰会，他们想听听你们的意见。

column5: It's basically the hub of Alestia.\nPorts from there go to the rest of the known world.\nA huge city of commerce, it's full of strange people.
column6: 它基本算是阿莱斯蒂亚的中心枢纽。\n那里的港口通往已知世界的各个角落。\n一座巨大的商业都市，满是形形色色的人。

column5: But you'd get stabbed in the back before you find help.\nThat's what puts people like me in business. Protectors of the weak.\nWell, not that I'm calling you weak, but you get the idea.
column6: 可你还没找到人帮忙，后背就先挨了一刀。\n这才有我们这行人的饭碗。弱者的守护者。\n呃，不是说你们弱，你懂我的意思。

column5: Because of its central location, it's the perfect meeting spot.\nThe Generals from Alarinthia and Balteus sail over annually.\nValinorth is non-partisan, so you usually sit this one out.
column6: 由于位置居中，那里是绝佳的会晤地点。\n来自阿拉林西亚和巴尔泰乌斯的将军每年都会渡海前来。\n瓦利诺斯保持中立，所以你们通常不参与。

column5: Maybe it's a chance to get Valinorth more invested in Alestian politics.\nBut they want your input, and I've been sent to pick you up.\nI guess it's a good thing I got here when I did, right?
column6: 也许这能让瓦利诺斯更多地参与阿莱斯蒂亚的政事。\n不过他们想听你们的意见，而我被派来接你们。\n我想我及时赶到，算是件好事，对吧？

column5: Look, I don't ask for specifics.\nI do this to get paid, and make a living.\nIf you want, feel free to ask them when we get there.
column6: 听着，我从不打听细节。\n我干这行是为了赚钱糊口。\n要是你想知道，等到了那里尽管问他们。

column5: That is, if you two even agree to follow me.\nBut right now, I can't let you die on my watch.\nWe'll discuss the rest once we're out of harm's way.
column6: 前提是，你们俩愿意跟我走。\n但眼下，我不能让你们在我眼皮底下送命。\n等我们脱离危险，再谈其余的事。

column5: Is that an accusation of some kind?\nWhere I come from, you don't accuse the guy with a bigger sword.\nI'll pretend I didn't hear that, and carry on with this search.
column6: 这算是什么指控吗？\n在我的家乡，你可不会去指控一个比你剑大的人。\n我就当没听见，继续搜查。

column5: Actually, I come from Alarinthia.\nPractically born with a blade in my hand.\nA figure of speech of course. Don't picture that.
column6: 其实，我来自阿拉林西亚。\n差不多一出生手里就攥着剑。\n当然，这只是打个比方。别去脑补那画面。

column5: Eventually you grow up, and need money of your own.\nI took the first ship to Mazeo and started selling my sword arm.\nI don't miss that place at all. It's disgustingly warm and humid.
column6: 等你长大，就得自己挣钱了。\n我搭上第一班船去了马泽奥，开始当佣兵，靠这把剑吃饭。\n我一点也不怀念那地方。又热又潮，让人难受。

column5: Completely different than what you'd think.\nWe recognize power, not lineage, or claim to the throne.\nOr, I guess {i}they{/i} do, since I no longer live there.
column6: 跟你想的完全不同。\n我们看重的是力量，而不是血脉或对王位的宣称。\n或者说，我想{i}他们{/i}是这样，毕竟我已不再住在那儿。

column5: Instead of elections, there's a tournament every few years.\nOnly the strongest tribe wins the right to rule Alarinthia.\nOf course, the rule is always contested shortly after.
column6: 我们不搞选举，而是每隔几年办一场比武大会。\n只有最强的部族才能赢得统治阿拉林西亚的权力。\n当然，那权力往往没过多久就被人挑战。

column5: It's good not to make any close friends.\nYou never know who you'll have to put to the blade.\nIt's a culture of war, and only the strongest prevail.
column6: 最好别交什么挚友。\n你永远不知道将来得把剑刺向谁。\n那是一种战争文化，唯有最强者才能立足。

column5: You don't have to suck up to me. I know it's awful.\nThat's basically why I left the first chance I got.\nI'd take a stable living over that chaotic place.
column6: 你不用讨好我。我知道那地方很糟。\n这差不多就是我一有机会就离开的原因。\n比起那个混乱之地，我宁愿过安稳日子。

column5: No offense, but you have it pretty easy here.\nThis is a paradise compared to what I had in Alarinthia.\nI mean, present circumstances excluded, of course.
column6: 别见怪，但你们这儿日子过得挺轻松。\n比起我在阿拉林西亚的生活，这里是天堂。\n当然，眼下的情形除外。

column5: The weak die out pretty fast, so not really.\nI'd say there's always a stable \"top ten\" list.\nIf someone isn't on it, they aren't worth your time.
column6: 弱者很快就淘汰了，所以也谈不上。\n要我说，那儿总有一份稳定的“前十”名单。\n要是不在名单上，就不值得你花时间。

column5: Very funny. A joke question. I'll pass.
column6: 真好笑。这是开玩笑的问题。我略过。

column5: Hey, we're talking about putting your life on the line.\nDo you really think you'd want protection from a nobody?
column6: 喂，我们说的可是拿命去拼的事。\n你真会想要一个无名小卒来保护你吗？

column5: As you can tell, I'm very passionate about this.\nComes with the territory of being in the top ten.\nThough after this, I hope to rise a few ranks.
column6: 你也看得出来，我对这事很有热情。\n跻身前十，自然就会有这份自觉。\n不过经此一事，我希望能再升几名。

column5: Congratulations. You're now on my nerves.\nLet's change the subject before I leave you behind.
column6: 恭喜。你惹到我了。\n在我把你甩下之前，换个话题吧。

column5: No, I'm with my true family in Mazeo.\nWe have a different concept of family in Alarinthia.\nYou choose your family, and members come and go.
column6: 不，我真正的家人在马泽奥。\n在阿拉林西亚，我们对家庭的观念不同。\n家人是你自己选的，成员来去无常。

column5: When I left Alarinthia, I left that family behind.\nI made a new one in Mazeo, and they're no less important.\nWe don't go by blood in Alarinthia, but by choice.
column6: 我离开阿拉林西亚时，也抛下了那个家。\n我在马泽奥组成了新的家，他们同样重要。\n在阿拉林西亚，我们不论血缘，而凭选择。

column5: Yeah, and sorry if that sounds weird to you.\nThere's a big culture difference at play here.\nPerhaps you'll learn more when we leave Valinorth.
column6: 是啊，要是这让你觉得奇怪，我很抱歉。\n这里面有很大的文化差异。\n也许等我们离开瓦利诺斯，你会了解更多。

column5: Not that I expect you to change your ways.\nBut it's always nice to learn about the world.\nAnyway, let's get back to the matter at hand.
column6: 我并不是指望你们改变自己的方式。\n但了解这个世界总是件好事。\n总之，我们回到正事上来吧。

column5: They died during one of Alarinthia's tournaments.\nWhat stung worse, is that they made it to the final round.\nAlarinthia holds tournaments for the throne, not elections.
column6: 他们死于阿拉林西亚的一场比武大会。\n更让人痛心的是，他们打进了决赛。\n阿拉林西亚靠比武大会定王位，而非选举。

column5: But that's not why I left the nation at all.\nI heard about this in a letter a few years back.\nHaven't been home since, and don't plan on going either.
column6: 但那根本不是我离开那个国家的原因。\n这事是我几年前在一封信里得知的。\n自那以后我再没回过家，也不打算回去。

column5: Alarinthia is quite far away.\nIt easily takes a few days to reach by sea.\nThe climate is so different, I almost can't explain it.
column6: 阿拉林西亚相当遥远。\n乘船也轻易要花上几天。\n那里的气候大不相同，我简直无法形容。

column5: Just, don't dress in layers.\nWear as little clothing as possible.\nYou're liable to melt into a puddle.
column6: 只是，别穿得一层又一层。\n尽量少穿点衣服。\n否则你会被热化成一滩水。

column5: Alarinthia is known for its cutthroat political landscape.\nEven then, extreme heat is the leading cause of death.\nI'm not joking. Go unprepared and you'll pay for it.
column6: 阿拉林西亚以残酷无情的政局著称。\n即便如此，酷热才是那里的头号死因。\n我不是开玩笑。毫无准备地去，你会付出代价。

column5: It's better to know beforehand, than go and regret it.\nWho knows where the path ahead might take you.\nJust doing my duty to help keep you safe.
column6: 与其去了后悔，不如事先了解。\n谁知道前路会把你们带向何方。\n我只是尽我的职责，帮你们保平安。

column5: Well, yeah, if The Triumvirate {i}is{/i} truly responsible.\nAlestia is divided into four nations, right?\nValinorth, Mazeo, Alarinthia, and Balteus.
column6: 嗯，是啊，如果三人执政团{i}真的{/i}是幕后黑手的话。\n阿莱斯蒂亚分为四个国家，对吧？\n瓦利诺斯、马泽奥、阿拉林西亚，还有巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: Each nation has a General that serves The Triumvirate.\nThey rule in their stead, and make sure everything runs smoothly.\nExcept — you guessed it. The Elder, or General, of Valinorth.
column6: 每个国家都有一位将军效命于三人执政团。\n他们代其统治，确保一切运转顺畅。\n唯独——你猜对了。瓦利诺斯的长老，或者说将军。

column5: No one really knows why you remained untouched for so long.\nBut the theory is that they don't want to anger the spirits.\nYou know, because of all that spiritual energy residing here.
column6: 没人真正知道你们为何长久以来未受侵扰。\n但有种说法是，他们不想触怒灵。\n你懂的，因为这里汇聚着那么多灵性力量。

column5: So I'm thinking this is a power play.\nTake the fourth nation, and control the whole world.\nThey did the same thing to Mazeo about twenty years ago.
column6: 所以我猜这是一场夺权之举。\n拿下第四个国度，就能掌控整个世界。\n大约二十年前，他们对马泽奥也做过同样的事。

column5: The same thing that's happening here, but with less fire.\nThey occupied the free town, and placed a General in charge.\nThey used terrible force, but the town improved because of it.
column6: 和这里发生的一样，只是没有那么多的火。\n他们占领了那座自由城，派了一位将军掌管。\n他们动用了可怕武力，但城市也因此变好了。

column5: I'll never agree with their methods, but Mazeo is peaceful.\nIf they're burning villages down now, though? Unforgivable.\nPerhaps The Rebellion isn't in the wrong, after all.
column6: 我永远不会认同他们的手段，但马泽奥确实和平。\n可要是他们如今在烧毁村庄？不可饶恕。\n也许反抗军终究并没有错。

column5: The way it looks right now? They already do.\nThat's why we need to get out of here as soon as possible.\nA stiff drink at Peregrino is sounding pretty good right now.
column6: 从现在的情况看？他们早就占了上风。\n所以我们得尽快离开这里。\n现在想想，去佩雷格里诺喝杯烈酒倒是不错。

column5: Let's hurry up and get this finished.\nIt's turned into a fool's errand, and I'm no fool.
column6: 咱们快点把这事了结吧。\n这已经变成一桩蠢差事，而我可不是蠢人。

column5: It's not like anything I've seen before.\nSo in tune with the spirits, you let them govern you.\nThe rest of Alestia has history in their own hands.
column6: 这跟我见过的任何地方都不一样。\n你们与灵如此契合，任由其主宰自己。\n而阿莱斯蒂亚的其他地方，历史都握在自己手中。

column5: Not that it's a bad thing, of course.\nIt's just different from the rest of the world.\nFrom what I've seen, the spirits have a good grasp on things.
column6: 当然，这并不是坏事。\n只是和世界其他地方不同罢了。\n依我所见，灵对事情把握得很好。

column5: Well, you're in the middle of a forest out here.\nYou know what they say about nature and spiritual energy.\nThe rest of the world has been deforested and settled differently.
column6: 嗯，你们身处森林中央。\n你们知道人们怎么说大自然与灵性力量。\n世界其他地方早已砍伐殆尽，被以不同方式开发定居。

column5: It's not that they don't care for spirits.\nActually, it's more like they don't know anything else.\nThey've lived their entire lives in areas devoid of spiritual energy.
column6: 并不是他们不在乎灵。\n其实，更像是他们对别的全然不知。\n他们一辈子都生活在毫无灵性力量的地方。

column5: But Valinorth is so peaceful, while the rest of the world isn't.\nIt might very well be the influence of the spirit realm.\nYou have a good thing going here. I can't stand what's happening.
column6: 可瓦利诺斯如此安宁，世界其他地方却不然。\n这很可能是灵界的影响。\n你们这里的日子过得很好。我实在无法忍受眼前发生的事。

column5: Well, let's not jump to conclusions.\nI'm a sellsword, there's no business in peace for me.\nAfter I retire though, it's always an option.
column6: 嗯，别急着下结论。\n我是个佣兵，太平盛世可没我的生意。\n不过等我退役了，也不失为一条出路。

column5: If I live long enough to retire, that is.\nMy business isn't exactly the safest in the world.\nWhat's going on here is pretty good proof of that.
column6: 前提是我能活到退休。\n我这行当可不算是世上最安全的。\n这儿发生的事就是很好的证明。

column5: This is it. This is what we needed!{w}\nI call over Ulric and Valessa, showing them what I found.{w}\nUlric seems tensed up, and even a little anxious.
column6: 就是这个。这正是我们需要的东西！{w}\n我把乌尔里克和瓦莱莎叫过来，给他们看我找到的东西。{w}\n乌尔里克似乎绷得很紧，甚至有些焦虑。

column5: So Mylus {i}was{/i} working with The Rebellion!\nApparently, he was sheltering a blade...?\nCould that be why they attacked us?
column6: 这么说迈勒斯{i}确实{/i}在和反抗军合作！\n据说，他还窝藏了一把剑……？\n难道这就是他们袭击我们的原因？

column5: Doing all this for a blade?\nLet's be realistic, Valessa.
column6: 做这一切就为了一把剑？\n现实点吧，瓦莱莎。

column5: It must've been very important.\nI'm assuming Mylus took it with him.\nI don't see any blades lying around here.
column6: 那一定非常重要。\n我猜迈勒斯把它带走了。\n我可没看见这儿有什么剑。

column5: But about this envoy he mentioned...?\nAnd this supposed \"special person\"?\nUlric, why did you lie to us?
column6: 可他提到的那位使者呢……？\n还有那个所谓的“特殊人物”？\n乌尔里克，你为什么要骗我们？

column5: It's true. Anybody would've figured it out by now.{w}\nHe seems to admit defeat and closes his eyes.{w}\nAlmost like he didn't want to see us as he spoke.
column6: 没错。事到如今，谁都能猜出来了。{w}\n他似乎认了输，闭上眼睛。{w}\n仿佛说话时不愿看着我们。

column5: We didn't think you'd come if you knew.\nI tried to hide it, but I guess there's no point anymore.\nAfter seeing this attack — I need to request your help.
column6: 我们想，要是你们知道实情就不会来。\n我本想瞒着，但看来现在已经没意义了。\n亲眼见到这场袭击之后——我需要请求你们的帮助。

column5: This is far from the first village they'll raze.\nThey're up to something much bigger.\nThat's why you wanted to come here, right?
column6: 这远不是他们要夷平的第一座村庄。\n他们图谋的事要大得多。\n你之所以想来这里，就是这个原因，对吧？

column5: Yeah, you're right.\nThere's little time to argue, and nowhere else to go.\nIt looks like you got what you needed, Ulric.
column6: 是啊，你说得对。\n没时间争论了，也无处可去。\n看来你得到了你想要的东西，乌尔里克。

column5: Let's get back to the Town Square.\nWe'll exit the village through Main Street.
column6: 我们回城镇广场去。\n从主街出村。

column5: We enter Mylus' house and immediately spread out.{w}\nAfter a few moments, it's evident that nobody is here.{w}\nUlric sighs, but Valessa isn't ready to give up.
column6: 我们走进迈勒斯的家，立刻分头搜查。{w}\n片刻之后，显然这里一个人也没有。{w}\n乌尔里克叹了口气，但瓦莱莎还不肯放弃。

column5: I don't know what you expected.\nYou think The Elder would just stay here...?\nI assume he's at The Grand Tree as well.
column6: 我不知道你指望什么。\n你以为长老会老老实实待在这儿……？\n我猜他也在巨树那儿。

column5: No, there has to be something here.\nIt's not him, but his books as well.\nHe must have some kind of record.
column6: 不，这里一定有什么。\n不光是他本人，还有他的书。\n他一定留有某种记录。

column5: Record of what, exactly?
column6: 到底是什么样的记录？

column5: Ulric, The Triumvirate is burning down Valinorth!\nThey seem to think we're caught up with The Rebels.\nThinking The Elder is clueless? That's stupid!
column6: 乌尔里克，三人执政团正在烧毁瓦利诺斯！\n他们似乎以为我们和反抗军有牵连。\n以为长老毫不知情？真是愚蠢！

column5: She walks over to the large window and looks outside.{w}\nWe're all relieved that the flames haven't reached us yet.{w}\nLooking through some papers, she whispers to herself.
column6: 她走到那扇大窗前，望向外面。{w}\n我们都松了口气，火焰还没蔓延到这里。{w}\n她翻看着一些文件，低声自言自语。

column5: Come on Mylus, give us something!\nYou're smarter than this, I know it.\nShipping manifests — anything!
column6: 别这样，迈勒斯，给我们留点线索啊！\n你比这聪明，我知道的。\n货运单——什么都行！

column5: With a renewed determination, Ulric examines the large table.{w}\nHe shuffles papers aside and flips through the books.{w}\nIt's almost like he's in a rush to find something first.
column6: 乌尔里克重新打起精神，检查起那张大桌子。{w}\n他把文件拨到一旁，翻开那些书。{w}\n简直像是急着要先找到什么似的。

column5: None of this is helping, Valessa!\nIt's everything you'd expect to find.
column6: 这些都没用，瓦莱莎！\n全都是意料之中的东西。

column5: No, there has to be something here!\nCome on Seer, give us a hand!
column6: 不，这里一定有什么东西！\n来吧，先知，帮我们一把！

column5: No, there has to be something here!\nCome on Seeress, give us a hand!
column6: 不，这里一定有什么东西！\n来吧，先知，帮我们一把！

column5: It is optional, but highly recommended that you talk to your comrades.
column6: 与同伴交谈是可选的，但强烈建议这么做。

column5: I walk over to the bookshelf and see what I can find.{w}\nIt seems to be full of books about the Spirit Realm, and Valinorth.{w}\nSomehow, I don't think either of these subjects will help.
column6: 我走到书架前，看看能找到什么。{w}\n上面似乎摆满了关于灵界和瓦利诺斯的书。{w}\n不知怎的，我觉得这两类书都帮不上忙。

column5: Eventually, I come across a book about The Rebellion.{w}\nI doubt it's what we need, but I decide to take a look.{w}\nAs I open it up, a piece of paper falls out.
column6: 终于，我翻到一本关于反抗军的书。{w}\n我怀疑这不是我们要找的，但还是决定看看。{w}\n我打开它时，一张纸片掉了出来。

column5: I walk over to the bookshelf and see what I can find.{w}\nIt seems to be full of books about the Spirit Realm, and Valinorth.{w}\nSomehow, I don't think either of these subjects will help.
column6: 我走到书架前，看看能找到什么。{w}\n上面似乎摆满了关于灵界和瓦利诺斯的书。{w}\n不知怎的，我觉得这两类书都帮不上忙。

column5: Eventually, I come across a book about The Rebellion.{w}\nI doubt it's what we need, but I decide to take a look.{w}\nAs I open it up, a piece of paper falls out.
column6: 终于，我翻到一本关于反抗军的书。{w}\n我怀疑这不是我们要找的，但还是决定看看。{w}\n我打开它时，一张纸片掉了出来。

column5: Hmm?
column6: 嗯？

column5: I wish. This whole place is a mess.\nHonestly, I don't even know what to look for.\nMylus isn't stupid though. He'd leave {i}something{/i}.
column6: 我倒希望如此。这地方一团糟。\n说实话，我连该找什么都不知道。\n不过迈勒斯不傻。他一定会留下{i}什么{/i}。

column5: Honestly, only a few months.\nHe was thrust into the position against his will.\nSomething happened to his Father, the previous Elder.
column6: 说实话，才几个月。\n他是被迫坐上这个位置的。\n他父亲，也就是上一任长老，出了事。

column5: But he's done such a good job, it's crazy.\nThe leadership of Valinorth did {i}not{/i} skip a beat!\nHe must've been training under his Father.
column6: 可他做得非常好，简直让人难以置信。\n瓦利诺斯的领导层{i}丝毫{/i}没有出现断层！\n他一定一直在父亲手下受训。

column5: Nobody knows, actually.\nHe went on a trip to Mazeo and never came back.\nSearch parties came up with nothing, it's like he vanished.
column6: 其实没人知道。\n他去马泽奥一趟，就再也没回来。\n搜索队一无所获，他就这样凭空消失了。

column5: Normally we'd hold an election, but things were crazy.\nThat, and Valinorth is really big on \"family\" and \"tradition\".\nEveryone just seemed to expect that Mylus would take over.
column6: 按惯例我们该举行选举，可当时局面太乱。\n再加上瓦利诺斯格外看重“家族”与“传统”。\n大家似乎都认定迈勒斯会继任。

column5: Sorry, I guess you're right.\nI'm not really treating this as \"real\".\nIt's something you learn to do early on.
column6: 抱歉，我想你说得对。\n我确实没把这一切当成“真的”。\n这是你从小就得学会的事。

column5: But this seems premeditated, to say the least.\nThe Triumvirate must've been planning this for a while.\nMylus taking over? I doubt that's directly related.
column6: 但至少可以说，这一切像是早有预谋。\n三人执政团一定谋划了许久。\n迈勒斯继任？我怀疑那没有直接关系。

column5: He's performed admirably for the position he's in.\nI doubt even a full election would find a better candidate.\nI was scared for a while, but he really filled the role.
column6: 以他的处境而言，他表现得相当出色。\n我怀疑就算举行完整的选举，也找不到更好的人选。\n我曾担心过一阵，但他确实胜任了这个角色。

column5: He didn't want to do it, but he kind of had to.\nIt all happened so fast, I'm not sure of the specifics.\nBut it was seamless, you almost couldn't notice.
column6: 他并不想这么做，但又不得不如此。\n一切都发生得太快，我不清楚细节。\n但过渡得毫无破绽，你几乎察觉不到。

column5: I guess, but we can't all get what we want.\nIt's not like I grew up wanting to be a Scribe.\nHe'll grow into the role, I'm sure of it.
column6: 也许吧，可我们没法都如愿以偿。\n我从小也没想过要当书记官。\n他会慢慢胜任这个角色的，我确信。

column5: But we can worry about that after this is over.\nThere's lots to do, and we can't even find him.\nI really hope that nothing bad has happened.
column6: 但这些等事情结束后再操心吧。\n有太多事要做，我们却连人都找不到。\n我真希望没有出什么坏事。

column5: Wait, you want to be the Elder?\nAre you sure you don't have a full plate right now?\nI mean, we could always try to find someone more willing.
column6: 等等，你想当长老？\n你确定现在你手头不是已经够忙了吗？\n我是说，我们总能找个更愿意的人。

column5: But we can worry about that after this is over.\nThere's lots to do, and we can't even find him.\nI really hope that nothing bad has happened.
column6: 但这些等事情结束后再操心吧。\n有太多事要做，我们却连人都找不到。\n我真希望没有出什么坏事。

column5: I agree, but I feel a bit sorry for him.\nYou can see it in his eyes, it stresses him out.\nMaybe we can find someone more willing, you know?
column6: 我同意，但我有点替他难过。\n从他眼神里就能看出来，这让他压力很大。\n也许我们能找个更愿意的人，你懂的？

column5: But we can worry about that after this is over.\nThere's lots to do, and we can't even find him.\nI really hope that nothing bad has happened.
column6: 但这些等事情结束后再操心吧。\n有太多事要做，我们却连人都找不到。\n我真希望没有出什么坏事。

column5: I'd want to get to the bottom of it, then.\nThere's more going on than we can take at face value.\nHe'd have his reasons, and I'd want to hear all of them.
column6: 那我就想把事情查个水落石出。\n这里面另有隐情，不能只看表面。\n他一定有自己的理由，而我想全部听他说清楚。

column5: That's the thing though, it's not actually happening.\nIf he can explain himself, and we can prevent this...?\nWell, then we can deal with it in a reasonable way.
column6: 可问题就在于，这一切其实并未发生。\n要是他能解释清楚，而我们又能阻止这一切……？\n那好，到时我们就能用理智的方式处理。

column5: We can't condemn him on a vision like this.\nThat's like hating someone for what they do in a dream.\nBesides, we have no way of confirming this is his fault.
column6: 我们不能凭这样一场幻象就给他定罪。\n那就好比因为某人梦里做的事去恨他。\n再说，我们也无从证实这是他的过错。

column5: And it's something I'd happily listen to.\nThat is, after we find a way to prevent this.\nI'm not passing judgement until I hear more.
column6: 而我也乐于听他说。\n前提是，我们先找到阻止这一切的办法。\n在听到更多之前，我不会妄下判断。

column5: We can't condemn him based on a vision like this.\nThat's like hating someone for what they do in a dream.\nBesides, we have no way of confirming this is his fault.
column6: 我们不能凭这样一场幻象就给他定罪。\n那就好比因为某人梦里做的事去恨他。\n再说，我们也无从证实这是他的过错。

column5: I'm making a pretty educated guess.\nI'm trained to detect this kind of stuff.\nBut it's so weird, because this feels like reality.
column6: 我是凭经验做了相当靠谱的推断。\n我受过训练，能察觉这类事物。\n可这太奇怪了，因为这里感觉就像现实。

column5: What's going to happen to me...?\nI mean technically, I'm not real, right?\nThat's hard to take in. This feels real to me.
column6: 我会怎么样呢……？\n我是说，严格来讲，我不是真实的，对吧？\n这很难接受。可对我来说，这一切都无比真实。

column5: But the way you're acting, yeah, it makes me certain.\nIt's very rare that I become lucid in a vision.\nBut with the evidence at hand, I'm very sure.
column6: 但看你的举止，对，这让我确信了。\n我在幻象中保持清醒的时刻极其罕见。\n但就现有证据来看，我非常确定。

column5: Better not talk about it too loud, though.\nWouldn't want Ulric to realize something is up.\nThe rules state that only you and I can know.
column6: 不过，最好别说得太大声。\n可不能让乌尔里克察觉出什么。\n规矩就是，此事只能你我知道。

column5: Trust me, it's better for him not to know.\nHe'd act recklessly, and he'd be really confused.\nWell, more reckless than normal, I mean.
column6: 相信我，他不知道最好。\n他会行事鲁莽，而且会彻底懵掉。\n呃，我是说，比平时更鲁莽。

column5: There's entire books written on this subject, you know.\nBut no one must know when they're in a vision.\nIt could screw up what the spirits want to show us.
column6: 你知道吗，关于这个主题有成书论述。\n但身处幻象中时，绝不能让旁人知道。\n那会搅乱灵想让我们看到的东西。

column5: These are gifts. Blessings, directly from the realm of spirits.\nWe're not in any position to harm what they give us.
column6: 这是恩赐。是来自灵界的祝福。\n我们无权去破坏它们给予我们的东西。

column5: As long as any other dream, I guess.\nOr maybe when the spirits decide you've seen enough.\nThat's one of the things we don't really know.
column6: 我猜，和寻常的梦一样长吧。\n或者，也许直到灵认为你看够了为止。\n这正是我们并不真正了解的事情之一。

column5: I guess something traumatic, like your death, would end it.\nOur minds aren't fit to comprehend what would happen next.\nWe should make the most of the time we {i}do{/i} have in here.
column6: 我猜，某种创伤性的事件，比如你的死亡，会终结它。\n我们的心智无法理解之后会发生什么。\n我们该好好利用在{i}这里{/i}所拥有的时间。

column5: Nobody knows, but we assume it's to protect us.\nIf we know what's coming, we can change what happens.\nSeers have done it time and time again for thousands of years.
column6: 没人知道，但我们猜想是为了保护我们。\n若我们知晓即将发生什么，就能改变结局。\n数千年来，先知们一次又一次做到了这点。

column5: A lot of people think they'll want something in exchange.\nThat they're planting seeds to reap later down the line.\nA stupid superstition if you ask me. They just want to help.
column6: 很多人以为它们会索取回报。\n以为它们在播种，日后好收割。\n要我说，这是愚蠢的迷信。它们只是想帮忙。

column5: Well, I guess we'll have to disagree on that!\nThere's nothing more pure than the spirits.\nThis gift is a truly beautiful thing.
column6: 好吧，看来这点上我们只能保留分歧了！\n没有什么比灵更纯净。\n这份恩赐真是美好至极。

column5: Yeah, I agree!\nThere's nothing more pure than the spirits.\nWithout the visions, we'd have died out ages ago.
column6: 是啊，我同意！\n没有什么比灵更纯净。\n没有这些幻象，我们早就灭绝了。

column5: This particular vision? No.\nBut the concept of visions in general? Yes.\nWithout them, we'd have gone extinct long ago.
column6: 这一场幻象？不算。\n但笼统地说，幻象这个概念本身？算。\n没有它们，我们早就灭绝了。

column5: They guide the world to a better future.\nAnd what's better, they ask for nothing in return.\nOnly that we continue to harness this amazing power.
column6: 它们引导世界走向更美好的未来。\n更难得的是，它们不求任何回报。\n只愿我们继续驾驭这份奇妙的力量。

column5: Yeah, it's just like I said. For better or worse.\nI was trained to be your Scribe from a young age.\nWe've been inseparable ever since.
column6: 是啊，就像我说的。无论好坏。\n我从小就受训做你的书记官。\n从那时起，我们就形影不离。

column5: It's not exactly what I grew up wanting.\nBut I'm not in a position to shun Valinorth's tradition.\nBesides, I could think of people {i}much{/i} worse to serve.
column6: 这并不完全是我从小心中的愿望。\n但我没有资格背弃瓦利诺斯的传统。\n再说，我想得出{i}远比这{/i}更糟的效忠对象。

column5: Actually, you're seeing them firsthand.\nImagine how confused you'd be without me.\nWe're supposed to guide you through these visions.
column6: 其实，你正亲眼见证着这一切。\n想象一下没有我你会有多困惑。\n我们的职责就是引领你走过这些幻象。

column5: But when you wake up, you also need to report to me.\nOr, I guess you can report to Mylus in these dire circumstances.\nEither way, I help you in here, and you report out there.
column6: 但你醒来后，也得向我汇报。\n或者，我想在这种情况下，你也能向迈勒斯汇报。\n总之，我在这里面帮你，你在外面汇报。

column5: If it weren't for me, you wouldn't remember this.\nYou'd wake up, shrug it off, and go about your day.\nImagine what would happen to Valinorth then.
column6: 要是没有我，你根本不会记得这一切。\n你会醒来，耸耸肩，照常过日子。\n想想那样瓦利诺斯会是什么下场。

column5: Of course not! We're two sides of the same coin!\nHonestly, I wouldn't be able to do anything without you.\nA Scribe would do little good without visions to inhabit.
column6: 当然不会！我们就像同一枚硬币的两面！\n说实话，没有你我也什么都做不了。\n没有幻象可供进入，书记官也派不上什么用场。

column5: Whoa, let's all make assumptions!\nI'm going to pretend I didn't hear that.\nWe work as a {i}team{/i}, we both help each other.
column6: 哇哦，大家可都开始妄加揣测了！\n我就当没听见好了。\n我们是{i}团队{/i}，彼此扶持。

column5: You'd be clueless if I didn't chime in earlier.\nI don't downplay your ability, and I expect the same.\nPerhaps you lose both memory {i}and{/i} manners in visions.
column6: 要不是我刚才插话，你还一头雾水呢。\n我没有贬低你的能力，也指望你别这么对我。\n也许你在幻象里连记忆{i}带{/i}礼数都丢了。
